Na hettha dvinnaṃ atthānaṃ atthantaratāparihāro yutto tesaṃ dvinnampi atthānaṃ sutabhāvadīpanena ekavisayattā, itarathā thero bhagavato desanāya sabbathā paṭiggahaṇe pacchimatthavasena samattho, purimatthavasena ca asamatthoti āpajjeyyāti.

The meaning of the term 'foremost' has already been stated. However, regarding phrases such as "among the learned," there are also other elders who are learned, mindful, endowed with wisdom, resolute, and attendants. But this venerable one, when learning the word of the Buddha, did so having established himself in the learning of a treasurer within the dispensation of the Ten-Powered One. Therefore, he became known as the foremost among the learned. Furthermore, this elder's mindfulness for retention, after having learned the word of the Buddha, was more powerful than that of other elders. Therefore, he became known as the foremost among the mindful. This very venerable one, standing on a single phrase and learning sixty thousand phrases, knows all the phrases according to the method taught by the Teacher. Therefore, he became known as the foremost among those endowed with wisdom. Moreover, that venerable one's energy in learning the word of the Buddha and his energy in reciting it were unlike that of others. Therefore, he became known as the foremost among the resolute. And when attending upon the Tathāgata, he did not attend in the same manner as other attendant monks. For others also attended upon the Tathāgata, but they were not able to attend having grasped the mind of the Buddhas. This elder, however, from the day he received the position of attendant, being one of aroused energy, attended having grasped the mind of the Tathāgata. Therefore, he became known as the foremost among attendants. "Skilled in meaning" means skilled in the meaning of what is spoken and in its purpose. "Dhamma" means the Dhamma of the Pāḷi, or, alternatively, various causes. "Expression" means a letter, because it makes the meaning clear. For although the meaning is made clear by a word, because a word is rooted in letters, it is said to be "made clear by a letter." Alternatively, because it makes the meaning clear, a sentence is also called 'expression' here. For by a sentence the meaning is made fully clear, whence it was said by the Venerable Mahākaccāyana, "He explains by means of expressions." "Linguistic analysis" means etymological explanation, or the five kinds of linguistic methods. Their inclusion here is fitting because they are a cause for understanding the meaning through the specific arrangement of words. "Sequence" means the connection of before and after, or the correlation of the latter part of a discourse with the earlier part. The connection is to be made thus: 'in a manner befitting the state of being praised for the fivefold skillfulness by the General of the Dhamma, and for the fivefold foremost positions by the Blessed One.' "The power of retention" means the power designated as retention, or power in retention; in both cases, the ability to retain is what is meant. "Showing" also has the meaning "for the purpose of showing." With the phrase 'neither deficient nor excessive in meaning or expression,' he states the effect of the emphasis. With 'not to be seen otherwise,' he states what is to be rejected. And 'not otherwise' means not otherwise than the manner in which it was heard from the presence of the Blessed One; it does not mean not otherwise than the manner in which it was taught by the Blessed One. For the teaching of the Blessed One is of inconceivable power. Thus, the statement made earlier, "Who is able to understand it in every way?" is supported. Otherwise, if one were able to hear it only in the manner it was taught by the Blessed One, that statement should not have been said. However, with the meaning as stated, the demonstration of the power of retention is not contradicted, since retention is intended in the sense of not conflicting with the manner in which it was heard. Otherwise, if one were able to retain it only in the manner it was taught by the Blessed One, it would contradict the statement made earlier. Here, the exclusion of one of the two meanings is not proper, as both meanings have a single domain in that they illuminate the fact of its having been heard. Otherwise, the fault would arise that the elder, in grasping the Blessed One's teaching in every way, is capable in terms of the latter meaning but incapable in terms of the former.

“Yo [M 1.0149] paro na hoti, so attā”ti vuttāya niyakajjhattasaṅkhātāya santatiyā pavattanako tividhopi me-saddo, tasmā kiñcāpi niyakajjhattasantativasena ekasmiṃ yevatthe me-saddo dissati, tathāpi karaṇasampadānasāminiddesavasena vijjamānavibhattibhedaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “tīsu atthesu dissatī”ti, tīsu vibhattiyatthesu attanā saññuttavibhattito dissatīti attho[V 1.0132]. Gāthābhigītanti gāthāya abhigītaṃ abhimukhaṃ gāyitaṃ. Abhojaneyyanti bhojanaṃ kātumanaraharūpaṃ. Abhigītapadassa kattupekkhattā mayāti attho. Evaṃ sesesupi yathārahaṃ. Sutasaddassa kammabhāvasādhanavasena dvādhippāyikapadattā yathāyogaṃ “mayā suta”nti ca “mama suta”nti ca atthadvaye yujjati.

The word 'me' is threefold, giving rise to the continuity designated as 'one's own internal self', which is spoken of as "That which is not other, is self." Therefore, although the word 'me' appears in the single sense relating to one's own internal continuity, it is nevertheless said, with reference to the existing distinctions of case endings for the instrumental, dative, and possessive, that "it appears in three meanings." The meaning is that it appears in three case-meanings due to the case ending connected with 'self'. "Sung to with a verse" (gāthābhigītaṃ) means sung to, sung towards, with a verse. "Unfit for consumption" (abhojaneyyaṃ) means of a nature unsuitable for eating. Because the word 'abhigīta' requires an agent, the meaning 'by me' (mayā) is to be understood. Similarly, in the remaining cases, it should be understood as is appropriate. Because the word 'suta' has two intentions, by way of its derivation in the sense of object (kamma) and state (bhāva), it is fitting in two meanings as appropriate: 'heard by me' (mayā sutaṃ) and 'my hearing' (mama sutaṃ).

Kiñcāpi upasaggo kiriyaṃ viseseti, jotakamattabhāvato pana satipi tasmiṃ sutasaddoyeva taṃ taṃ atthaṃ vadatīti anupasaggassa sutasaddassa atthuddhāre saupasaggassa gahaṇaṃ na virujjhatīti āha “saupasaggo ca anupasaggo cā”ti. Assāti sutasaddassa. Upasaggavasenapi dhātusaddo visesatthavācako yathā “anubhavati parābhavatī”ti vuttaṃ “gacchantoti attho”ti. Tathā anupasaggopi dhātusaddo saupasaggo viya visesatthavācakoti āha “vissutadhammassāti attho”ti. Evamīdisesu. Sotaviññeyyanti sotadvāranissitena viññāṇena viññātabbaṃ, sasambhārakathā vā esā, sotadvārena viññātabbanti attho. Sotadvārānusāraviññātadharoti sotadvārānusārena manoviññāṇena viññātadhammadharo. Na hi sotadvāranissitaviññāṇamattena dhammo viññāyati, atha kho tadanusāramanoviññāṇeneva, sutadharoti ca tathā viññātadhammadharo vutto, tasmā tadatthoyeva sambhavatīti evaṃ vuttaṃ. Kammabhāvasādhanāni sutasadde sambhavantīti dassetuṃ “idha panā”tiādimāha. Pubbāparapadasambandhavasena atthassa upapannatā, anupapannatā ca viññāyati, tasmā sutasaddasseva vasena ayamattho “upapanno, anupapanno”ti vā na viññātabboti codanāya pubbāparapadasambandhavasena etadatthassa upapannataṃ dassetuṃ “me-saddassa hī”tiādi vuttaṃ. Mayāti atthe satīti kattutthe karaṇaniddesavasena mayāti atthe vattabbe sati, yadā me-saddassa kattuvasena karaṇaniddeso, tadāti vuttaṃ hoti. Mamāti atthe satīti sambandhīyatthe sāminiddesavasena [M 1.0150] mamāti atthe vattabbe sati, yadā sambandhavasena sāmi niddeso, tadāti vuttaṃ hoti.

Although a prefix qualifies an action, due to its nature of being merely an illuminator, even when the prefix is present, it is only the word 'suta' that conveys that very meaning. Therefore, in deriving the meaning of the unprefixed word 'suta', the inclusion of the prefixed word 'suta' is not contradicted. Thus, the Commentator said, 'both with a prefix and without a prefix.' 'Of it' (assa) means of the word 'suta'. By the power of a prefix, a verbal root can also express a specific meaning, for example, anubhavati (experiences) and parābhavati (oppresses). Therefore, it was said, 'the meaning is 'going'.’ Likewise, a verbal root without a prefix, like one with a prefix, can express a specific meaning. Thus, he said, 'the meaning is 'of one whose Dhamma is renowned'.' Thus it should be understood in cases like these. 'Cognizable by the ear' (sotaviññeyya) means to be cognized by consciousness dependent on the ear-door; or, this is a statement with its components, meaning it is to be cognized through the ear-door. 'One who bears what is cognized by following upon the ear-door' (sotadvārānusāraviññātadharo) means one who bears the Dhamma that has been cognized by mind-consciousness that follows upon the ear-door. For the Dhamma is not cognized merely by consciousness dependent on the ear-door, but rather only by the mind-consciousness that follows upon it. And 'one who has heard' (sutadharo) is said to be one who bears the Dhamma cognized in such a way. Therefore, only that meaning is possible; thus it was said. To show that derivations in the objective sense (kamma-sādhana) and the stative sense (bhāva-sādhana) are possible for the word 'suta', the Commentator said, 'But here...' and so on. The suitability or unsuitability of a meaning is known through the connection of preceding and following words. Therefore, in response to the objection that this meaning should not be understood as 'suitable' or 'unsuitable' merely by the power of the word 'suta' itself, it was said, 'For of the word me...' and so on, to show the suitability of this meaning through the connection of preceding and following words. Regarding 'when the meaning is mayā (by me)': when the agentive meaning mayā is to be expressed by way of indicating the instrumental case, when the word me is an indication of the instrumental case in the agentive sense, then this is the intended meaning. Regarding 'when the meaning is mama (of me)': when the relational meaning mama is to be expressed by way of indicating the genitive case, when it is an indication of the genitive case in the relational sense, then this is the intended meaning.

Evaṃ saddato ñātabbamatthaṃ viññāpetvā idāni tehi dassetabbamatthaṃ nidassento “evametesū”tiādimāha. Sutasaddasannidhāne payuttena evaṃ-saddena savanakiriyājotakeneva bhavitabbaṃ vijjamānatthassa jotakamattattā nipātānanti vuttaṃ “evanti sotaviññāṇādiviññāṇakiccanidassana”nti. Savanāya eva hi ākāro, nidassanaṃ, avadhāraṇampi, tasmā yathāvutto evaṃ-saddassa tividhopi attho savanakiriyājotakabhāvena idhādhippetoti. Ādi-saddena cettha sampaṭicchanādīnaṃ sotadvārikaviññāṇānaṃ, tadabhinipātānañca manodvārika [V 1.0133] viññāṇānaṃ gahaṇaṃ veditabbaṃ, yato sotadvārānusāraviññātatthe idha sutasaddoti vutto. Avadhāraṇaphalattā saddapayogassa sabbampi vākyaṃ antogadhāvadhāraṇaṃ, tasmā “suta”nti etassa sutamevāti ayamattho labbhatīti āha “assavanabhāvapaṭikkhepato”ti. Etena hi vacanena avadhāraṇena nirākataṃ dasseti. Yathā pana yaṃ sutaṃ sutamevāti niyametabbaṃ, tathā ca taṃ sutaṃ sammā sutaṃ hotīti avadhāraṇaphalaṃ dassetuṃ vuttaṃ “anūnādhikāviparītaggahaṇanidassana”nti. Atha vā saddantaratthāpohanavasena saddo atthaṃ vadati, tasmā “suta”nti etassa asutaṃ na hotīti ayamattho labbhatīti sandhāya “assavanabhāvapaṭikkhepato”ti vuttaṃ, iminā diṭṭhādinivattanaṃ karoti diṭṭhādīnaṃ “asuta”nti saddantaratthabhāvena nivattetabbattā. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – na idaṃ mayā attano ñāṇena diṭṭhaṃ, na ca sayambhuñāṇena sacchikataṃ, atha kho sutaṃ, tañca kho sutaṃ sammadevāti. Tadeva sammā sutabhāvaṃ sandhāyāha “anūnā…pe… dassana”nti. Hoti cettha –

Having thus explained the meaning to be known from the words, now, indicating the meaning to be shown by them, he said, 'Evaṃ me sutaṃ...' and so on. When used in the proximity of the word 'suta', the word 'evaṃ' must be one that only illuminates the act of hearing, because particles are merely illuminators of an existing meaning. Therefore, it was said, ''Evaṃ' is an indication of the function of consciousness, such as ear-consciousness and so on.' For it is indeed the manner, the indication, and also the affirmation for hearing. Therefore, the threefold meaning of the word 'evaṃ', as stated, is intended here in its capacity of illuminating the act of hearing. And here, by the word 'and so on', the inclusion of the ear-door consciousnesses beginning with receiving, and of the mind-door consciousnesses that impinge upon them, should be understood. For this reason, the word 'suta' is used here in the sense of what is cognized by following upon the ear-door. Because the use of the word has affirmation as its result, the entire sentence contains an implicit affirmation. Therefore, from this word 'suta', the meaning 'heard only' is obtained. Thus, he said, 'by the rejection of the state of not-hearing.' For by this word of affirmation, he shows what is rejected. Just as what is heard should be determined as 'heard only', so too, to show the result of the affirmation—that what is heard is rightly heard—it was said, 'an indication of the grasping without deficiency, excess, or distortion.' Alternatively, a word conveys its meaning by way of excluding the meaning of other words. Therefore, with reference to the fact that from this word 'suta' the meaning 'it is not unheard' is obtained, it was said, 'by the rejection of the state of not-hearing.' By this, he effects the exclusion of 'seen', etc., because 'seen', etc., are to be excluded by being the meaning of another word, 'unheard'. This is what is meant: This was not seen by me with my own knowledge, nor was it realized with self-originated knowledge, but rather it was heard; and that which was heard was heard rightly. Referring to that very state of being rightly heard, he said, 'without deficiency... an indication.' And here there is this verse:

“Evādisattiyā ceva, aññatthāpohanena ca;

Dvidhā saddo atthantaraṃ, nivatteti yathāraha”nti.

By the power of words such as 'evaṃ', and by the exclusion of another's meaning, a word in two ways appropriately excludes another meaning.

Apica avadhāraṇatthe evaṃ-sadde ayamatthayojanā karīyatīti tadapekkhassa sutasaddassa sāvadhāraṇattho vutto “assavanabhāvapaṭikkhepato”ti, tadavadhāraṇaphalaṃ dasseti “anū…pe… dassana”nti iminā. Savana-saddo cettha bhāvasaddena yogato kammasādhano veditabbo “suyyatī”ti. Anūnādhikatāya bhagavato sammukhā sutākārato aviparītaṃ[M 1.0151], aviparītassa vā suttassa gahaṇaṃ, tassa nidassanaṃ tathā, iti savanahetu suṇantapuggalasavanavisesavasena ayaṃ yojanā katā.

Furthermore, this explanation of meaning is made when the word 'evaṃ' is in the sense of affirmation. Therefore, for the word 'suta' which is dependent on it, the meaning with affirmation is stated as 'by the rejection of the state of not-hearing.' By this phrase 'without deficiency... an indication,' he shows the result of that affirmation. And here, the word 'savana' (hearing), due to its connection with the word 'bhāva' (state), should be understood as a derivation in the objective sense, as in 'it is heard' (suyyati). Due to being without deficiency or excess, it is undistorted from the manner in which it was heard in the presence of the Blessed One; or, it is the grasping of the undistorted sutta. The indication of that is likewise. Thus, this explanation is made according to the specific hearing of the listening person, with hearing as the cause.

Evaṃ padattayassa ekena pakārena atthayojanaṃ dassetvā idāni pakārantarenāpi taṃ dassetuṃ “tathā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha tassāti yā bhagavato sammukhā dhammassavanākārena pavattā manodvārikaviññāṇavīthi, tassā. Sā hi nānāppakārena ārammaṇe pavattituṃ samatthā, na sotadvārika viññāṇavīthi ekārammaṇeyeva pavattanato, tathā ceva vuttaṃ “sotadvārānusārenā”ti. Tena hi sotadvārikaviññāṇavīthi nivattati. Nānappakārenāti vakkhamānena anekavihitena byañjanatthaggahaṇākārasaṅkhātena nānāvidhena ākārena, etena imissā yojanāya ākārattho evaṃ-saddo gahitoti dasseti. Pavattibhāvappakāsananti pavattiyā atthibhāvappakāsanaṃ. Yasmiṃ pakāre vuttappakārā viññāṇavīthi nānappakārena pavattā, tadeva ārammaṇaṃ sandhāya “dhammappakāsana”nti [V 1.0134] vuttaṃ, na pana sutasaddassa dhammatthaṃ, tena vuttaṃ “ayaṃ dhammo suto”ti. Tassā hi viññāṇavīthiyā ārammaṇameva “ayaṃ dhammo suto”ti vuccati. Tañca niyamiyamānaṃ yathāvuttāya viññāṇavīthiyā ārammaṇabhūtaṃ suttameva. Ayañhetthātiādi vuttassevatthassa pākaṭīkaraṇaṃ. Tappākaṭīkaraṇattho hettha hi-saddo. Viññāṇavīthiyā karaṇabhūtāya mayā na aññaṃ kataṃ, idaṃ pana ārammaṇaṃ kataṃ. Kiṃ pana tanti ce? Ayaṃ dhammo sutoti. Ayaṃ panetthādhippāyo – ākāratthe evaṃ-sadde “ekenākārenā”ti yo ākāro vutto, so atthato sotadvārānusāraviññāṇavīthiyā nānappakārena ārammaṇe pavattibhāvoyeva, tena ca tadārammaṇabhūtassa dhammasseva savanaṃ kataṃ, na aññanti. Evaṃ savanakiriyāya karaṇakattukammaviseso imissā yojanāya dassito.

Having thus shown the application of the meaning of the group of three words in one way, now, in order to show it also in another way, the words beginning with 'tathā' were spoken. Therein, 'tassā' refers to that mind-door cognitive process which arose from the presence of the Blessed One in the manner of hearing the Dhamma. For that process is capable of arising in many various ways in relation to an object; the ear-door cognitive process is not, because it arises only in relation to a single object. For that very reason, it was said, 'in accordance with the ear-door.' By that, the ear-door cognitive process is excluded. 'In many various ways' means in many various modes, to be explained, manifoldly arranged, designated as the mode of grasping the phrasing and the meaning. By this, it is shown that in this application, the word 'evaṃ' is taken as having the meaning of 'mode.' 'Revealing the state of occurrence' means making known the existence of the occurrence. With reference to that very object in which mode the cognitive process of the aforementioned kind arose in many various ways, it was said 'revealing the Dhamma'; but it was not said with reference to the meaning 'Dhamma' of the word 'suta.' Therefore, it was said, 'This Dhamma was heard.' For the very object of that cognitive process is called 'This Dhamma was heard.' And that, being determined, is the Sutta itself, which has become the object of the aforementioned cognitive process. The passage beginning with 'Ayañhettha' is a clarification of the meaning already stated. Herein, the particle 'hi' has the meaning of clarifying that. By me, with the cognitive process as the instrument, no other was made the object; but this was made the object. And if one should ask, 'What is that?'—'This Dhamma was heard.' But this is the intention here: in the word 'evaṃ' which has the meaning of 'mode,' whichever mode was spoken of as 'in one mode,' that mode, in terms of meaning, is precisely the state of occurrence in many various ways in relation to the object of the cognitive process that accords with the ear-door. And by that, the hearing of only the Dhamma which had become its object was done, and nothing else. Thus, in this application, the distinction of instrument, agent, and object of the act of hearing is shown.

Aññampi yojanamāha “tathā”tiādinā. Nidassanatthaṃ evaṃ-saddaṃ gahetvā nidassanena ca nidassitabbassāvinābhāvato “evanti nidassitabbappakāsana”nti vuttaṃ. Iminā hi tadavinābhāvato evaṃsaddena sakalampi suttaṃ paccāmaṭṭhanti dasseti, sutasaddassa kiriyāparattā, savanakiriyāya ca sādhāraṇaviññāṇappabandhapaṭibaddhattā tasmiñca viññāṇappabandhe [M 1.0152] puggalavohāroti vuttaṃ “puggalakiccappakāsana”nti. Sādhāraṇaviññāṇappabandho hi paṇṇattiyā idha puggalo nāma, savanakiriyā pana tassa kiccaṃ nāma. Na hi puggalavohārarahite dhammappabandhe savanakiriyā labbhati vohāravisayattā tassā kiriyāyāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. “Ida”ntiādi piṇḍatthadassanaṃ mayāti yathāvuttaviññāṇappabandhasaṅkhātapuggalabhūtena mayā. Sutanti savanakiriyāsaṅkhātena puggalakiccena yojitaṃ, imissā pana yojanāya puggalabyāpāravisayassa puggalassa, puggalabyāpārassa ca nidassanaṃ katanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

He states another application with the words beginning 'tathā.' Taking the word 'evaṃ' as having the meaning of 'demonstration,' and because of the inseparability of the demonstrated from the demonstration, it was said, '“Evaṃ” is the revealing of what is to be demonstrated.' By this, he shows that because of its inseparability from that, the entire Sutta is referred to by the word 'evaṃ.' And because the word 'suta' pertains to action, and because the act of hearing is connected to the common continuum of consciousness, and in that continuum of consciousness there is the conventional designation 'person,' it was said, 'revealing the function of a person.' For the common continuum of consciousness is here called 'person' by concept, and the act of hearing is called his 'function.' The act of hearing is not obtained in a continuum of phenomena devoid of the conventional designation 'person,' because that action has conventional designation as its domain; thus it should be understood. The passage beginning with 'Idaṃ' is a demonstration of the summary meaning. 'Mayā' means by me, who has become the person designated as the aforementioned continuum of consciousness. 'Sutaṃ' is connected with the function of a person, designated as the act of hearing. But in this application, a demonstration is made of the person who is the domain of a person's activity, and of the person's activity; thus it should be understood.

Ākāratthameva evaṃ-saddaṃ gahetvā purimayojanāya aññathāpi atthayojanaṃ dassetuṃ “tathā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Cittasantānassāti yathāvuttaviññāṇappabandhassa. Nānākārappavattiyāti nānappakārena ārammaṇe pavattiyā. Nānappakāraṃ atthabyañjanassa gahaṇaṃ, nānappakārassa vā atthabyañjanassa gahaṇaṃ tathā, tatoyeva sā “ākārapaññattī”ti vuttāti tadevatthaṃ samattheti “evanti hī”tiādinā. Ākārapaññattīti ca upādāpaññattiyeva, dhammānaṃ pana pavattiākāramupādāya paññattattā tadaññāya upādāpaññattiyā visesanatthaṃ “ākārapaññattī”ti vuttā visayaniddesoti uppattiṭṭhānaniddeso. Sotabbabhūto hi dhammo savanakiriyākattubhūtassa puggalassa savanakiriyāvasena pavattiṭṭhānaṃ kiriyāya kattukammaṭṭhattā tabbasena ca tadādhārassāpi dabbassa ādhārabhāvassa icchitattā, idha pana kiriyāya kattupavattiṭṭhānabhāvo icchitoti kammameva [V 1.0135] ādhāravasena vuttaṃ, tenāha “kattu visayaggahaṇasanniṭṭhāna”nti, ārammaṇameva vā visayo. Ārammaṇañhi tadārammaṇikassa pavattiṭṭhānaṃ. Evampi hi attho suviññeyyataro hoti. Yathāvuttavacane piṇḍatthaṃ dassetuṃ “ettāvatā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Ettāvatā ettakena yathāvuttatthena padattayena, kataṃ hotīti sambandho. Nānākārappavattenāti nānappakārena ārammaṇe pavattena. Cittasantānenāti yathāvuttaviññāṇavīthisaṅkhātena cittappabandhena. Gahaṇasadde cetaṃ karaṇaṃ. Cittasantānavinimuttassa kassaci kattu paramatthato abhāvepi saddavohārena buddhiparikappitabhedavacanicchāya cittasantānato aññamiva taṃsamaṅgiṃ katvā abhedepi bhedavohārena “cittasantānena taṃsamaṅgino”ti vuttaṃ. Vohāravisayo hi saddo nekantaparamatthikoti [M 1.0153] (kārakarūpasiddhiyaṃ yo kāreti sahetusuttaṃ passitabbaṃ) savanakiriyāvisayopi sotabbadhammo savanakiriyāvasena pavattacittasantānassa idha paramatthato kattubhāvato tassa visayoyevāti vuttaṃ “kattu visayaggahaṇasanniṭṭhāna”nti.

Taking the word 'evaṃ' in the sense of mode, it is said 'tathā,' and so on, to show a different interpretation of the meaning from the previous construction. 'Of the continuity of mind' refers to the stream of consciousness as previously stated. 'By the occurrence in various modes' means by the occurrence in the object in various ways. The grasping of meaning and expression in various ways, or the grasping of various kinds of meaning and expression, is likewise. Therefore, it is called 'designation of mode'; thus, that very meaning is supported by 'evaṃ hi,' and so on. And 'designation of mode' is indeed a designation based on conditioning; however, since it is designated by taking the mode of occurrence of phenomena as its basis, it is called 'designation of mode' to distinguish it from other designations based on conditioning. The exposition of the object is the exposition of the place of arising. For the audible phenomenon is the place of occurrence for the person who is the agent of the act of hearing, by way of the act of hearing, because the act has its standing in the agent and object, and by that means, the state of being a basis for a substance which is also its support is desired. Here, however, the state of being the agent's place of occurrence in the act is intended, so only the object is mentioned by way of a basis. Hence, he said, 'the conclusion of the grasping of the agent's object.' Or, the object itself is the domain. For the object is the place of occurrence for that which has it as its object. Even in this way, the meaning is more easily understood. To show the condensed meaning in the previously stated words, it is said, 'ettāvatā,' and so on. The connection is to be made thus: 'by this much' (ettāvatā), that is, by this much of the three words with the meaning as stated, 'it is done.' 'By the occurrence in various modes' means by that which occurs in the object in various ways. 'By the continuity of mind' means by the stream of mind, described as the previously stated consciousness-process. And this is the instrument in relation to the word 'grasping.' Even though, in an ultimate sense, there is no agent separate from the continuity of mind, by verbal convention, through the desire to express a distinction conceived by the intellect, having treated the one endowed with it as if other than the continuity of mind, it is said, 'of the one endowed with it, by the continuity of mind' through conventional distinction even when there is no distinction. For the word has convention as its domain; it is not exclusively ultimate. The audible phenomenon, which is the object of the act of hearing, is here, in an ultimate sense, the object of the continuity of mind occurring by way of the act of hearing, because of its being the agent; therefore, it is said, 'the conclusion of the grasping of the agent's object.'

Apica savanavasena cittappavattiyā eva savanakiriyābhāvato taṃvasena tadaññanāmarūpadhammasamudāyabhūtassa taṃkiriyākattu ca visayo hotīti katvā tathā vuttaṃ. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – purimanaye savanakiriyā, takkattā ca paramatthato tathāpavattacittasantānameva, tasmā kiriyāvisayopi “kattu visayo”ti vutto. Pacchimanaye pana tathāpavattacittasantānaṃ kiriyā, tadaññadhammasamudāyo pana kattā, tasmā kāmaṃ ekantato kiriyāvisayoyevesa dhammo, tathāpi kiriyāvasena “tabbantakattu visayo”ti vuttoti. Taṃsamaṅginoti tena cittasantānena samaṅgino. Kattūti kattārassa. Visayoti ārammaṇavasena pavattiṭṭhānaṃ, ārammaṇameva vā. Sutākārassa ca therassa sammā nicchitabhāvato “gahaṇasanniṭṭhāna”nti vuttaṃ.

Furthermore, it is said thus for this reason: since the very occurrence of mind by way of hearing is the act of hearing, by that means the agent of that act—the person who is the aggregate of other name-and-form phenomena—is also the object. This is what is meant: in the former method, the act of hearing and its agent are, in an ultimate sense, just the continuity of mind occurring in that way; therefore, even the object of the action is called 'the object of the agent.' In the latter method, however, the continuity of mind occurring in that way is the action, while the aggregate of other phenomena is the agent. Therefore, although this phenomenon is indeed exclusively the object of the action, it is nevertheless called 'the object of the agent possessing it' by way of the action. 'Of one endowed with that' means of one endowed with that continuity of mind. 'Of the agent' means of the agent. 'Object' means the place of occurrence by way of the object, or the object itself. And because it was rightly ascertained by the Elder who has the mode of what was heard, it is called 'the firm conclusion of grasping.'

Aparo nayo – yassa…pe… ākārapaññattīti ākāratthena evaṃ-saddena yojanaṃ katvā tadeva avadhāraṇatthampi gahetvā imasmiṃyeva naye yojetuṃ “gahaṇaṃ kataṃ” icceva avatvā “gahaṇasanniṭṭhānaṃ kata”nti vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Avadhāraṇena hi sanniṭṭhānamidhādhippetaṃ, tasmā “ettāvatā”tiādinā avadhāraṇatthampi evaṃ-saddaṃ gahetvā ayameva yojanā katāti dassetīti veditabbaṃ, imissā pana yojanāya gahaṇākāragāhakatabbisayavisesanidassanaṃ katanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Another method: for which... (the designation of mode) is by connecting the word 'evaṃ' with the sense of mode, and taking that same word also in the sense of determination, to apply it in this very method, it should be seen that it is said 'the firm conclusion of grasping is made' instead of merely saying 'the grasping is done.' For here, firm conclusion is intended by determination. Therefore, it should be understood that by taking the word 'evaṃ' also in the sense of determination with phrases like 'ettāvatā,' it shows that this very connection was made. Moreover, it should be seen that by this interpretation, an illustration of the distinction of the mode of grasping, the grasper, and its object is made.

Aññampi yojanamāha “atha vā”tiādinā. Pubbe attanā sutānaṃ nānāvihitānaṃ suttasaṅkhātānaṃ atthabyañjanānaṃ upadhāritarūpassa ākārassa nidassanassa, avadhāraṇassa vā pakāsanasabhāvo evaṃ-saddoti tadākārādibhūtassa upadhāraṇassa puggalapaññattiyā upādānabhūtadhammappabandhabyāpāratāya [V 1.0136] “puggalakiccaniddeso”ti vuttaṃ attanā sutānañhi atthabyañjanānaṃ puna upadhāraṇaṃ ākārādittayaṃ, tañca evaṃ-saddassa attho. So pana yaṃ dhammappabandhaṃ upādāya puggalapaññatti pavattā, tassa byāpārabhūtaṃ kiccameva[M 1.0154], tasmā evaṃ-saddena puggalakiccaṃ niddisīyatīti. Kāmaṃ savanakiriyā puggalabyāpāropi avisesena, tathāpi visesato viññāṇabyāpārovāti vuttaṃ “viññāṇakiccaniddeso”ti. Tathā hi puggalavādīnampi savanakiriyā viññāṇanirapekkhā natthi savanādīnaṃ visesato viññāṇabyāpārabhāvena icchitattā. Meti saddappavattiyā ekanteneva sattavisayattā, viññāṇakiccassa ca sattaviññāṇānamabhedakaraṇavasena tattheva samodahitabbato “ubhayakiccayuttapuggalaniddeso”ti vuttaṃ. “Aya”ntiādi tappākaṭīkaraṇaṃ. Ettha hi savanakiccaviññāṇasamaṅgināti evaṃ-saddena niddiṭṭhaṃ puggalakiccaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, taṃ pana puggalassa savanakiccaviññāṇasamaṅgībhāvena puggalakiccaṃ nāmāti dassetuṃ “puggalakiccasamaṅginā”ti avatvā “savanakiccaviññāṇasamaṅginā”ti āha, tasmā “puggalakicca”nti niddiṭṭhasavanakiccavatā viññāṇena samaṅgināti attho. Viññāṇavasena, laddhasavanakiccavohārenāti ca sutasaddena niddiṭṭhaṃ viññāṇakiccaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Savanameva kiccaṃ yassāti tathā. Savanakiccanti vohāro savanakiccavohāro, laddho so yenāti tathā. Laddhasavanakiccavohārena viññāṇasaṅkhātena vasena sāmatthiyenāti attho. Ayaṃ pana sambandho – savanakiccaviññāṇasamaṅginā puggalena mayā laddhasavanakiccavohārena viññāṇavasena karaṇabhūtena sutanti.

He states another interpretation with 'or alternatively,' and so on. The word 'evaṃ' has the nature of revealing the mode (ākāra), the indication (nidassana), or the ascertainment (avadhāraṇa) of the form that has been borne in mind of the meanings and expressions, designated as suttas, of various kinds, previously heard by oneself. Thus, it is called 'the indication of a person's function' because of the operation of that bearing in mind—which has that mode, etc., as its basis—in the continuum of phenomena that is the basis for the designation of a person. Indeed, the bearing in mind again of the meanings and expressions heard by oneself is the triad beginning with 'mode', and that is the meaning of the word 'evaṃ'. However, that meaning is precisely the function which is the operation of that continuum of phenomena depending on which the designation of a person proceeds. Therefore, by the word 'evaṃ', the person's function is indicated. Granted, the act of hearing is also a person's operation in a general sense; nevertheless, it is specifically an operation of consciousness. Therefore, it is said to be 'the indication of consciousness's function'. Indeed, it is so. For even in the view of the Personalists, the act of hearing is not independent of consciousness, because hearing and so on are desired to be specifically an operation of consciousness. Because the occurrence of the word 'me' pertains exclusively to the sphere of a being, and because the function of consciousness is to be included right there by way of not making a distinction between the being and the consciousness, it is called 'the indication of a person connected with both functions'. The passage beginning with 'Ayaṃ' is its clarification. For here, the phrase 'endowed with consciousness that has the function of hearing' is stated with reference to the person's function indicated by the word 'evaṃ'. However, to show that this is called the person's function because the person is endowed with consciousness that has the function of hearing, instead of saying 'endowed with the person's function', he said 'endowed with consciousness that has the function of hearing'. Therefore, the meaning is: endowed with consciousness that possesses the indicated function of hearing. And the phrase 'by way of consciousness, which has acquired the designation "function of hearing"' is stated with reference to the function of consciousness indicated by the word 'suta'. That [consciousness] for which hearing alone is the function is so called. The designation 'function of hearing' is savanakiccavohāro. That by which this designation is acquired is so called. The meaning is: by the power, called consciousness, which has acquired the designation 'function of hearing'. However, this is the connection: 'It was heard' (sutaṃ) 'by me' (mayā), the person endowed with consciousness that has the function of hearing, by means of consciousness, which is the instrument and has acquired the designation 'function of hearing'.

Apica “eva”nti saddassattho avijjamānapaññatti, “suta”nti saddassattho vijjamānapaññatti, tasmā te tathārūpapaññatti upādānabhūtapuggalabyāpārabhāveneva dassento āha “evanti puggalakiccaniddeso. Sutanti viññāṇakiccaniddeso”ti. Na hi paramatthatoyeva niyamiyamāne sati puggalakiccaviññāṇakiccavasena ayaṃ vibhāgo labbhatīti. Imissā pana yojanāya kattubyāpārakaraṇabyāpārakattuniddeso katoti veditabbo.

Furthermore, the meaning of the word 'evaṃ' is a designation of the non-existent, and the meaning of the word 'sutaṃ' is a designation of the existent. Therefore, wishing to show those designations solely as being the operation of a person which is their basis, he said: 'Evaṃ' is the indication of a person's function; 'Sutaṃ' is the indication of consciousness's function. For when considering things strictly in terms of ultimate reality, this division by way of a person's function and consciousness's function is not obtained. However, by this interpretation, it should be understood that an indication of the agent's operation, the instrument's operation, and the agent has been made.

Sabbassāpi saddādhigamanīyassa atthassa paññattimukheneva paṭipajjitabbattā, sabbāsañca paññattīnaṃ vijjamānādivasena chasu paññattibhedesu antogadhattā tāsu “eva”ntiādīnaṃ paññattīnaṃ sarūpaṃ niddhāretvā dassento “evanti cā”tiādimāha. Tattha “eva”nti ca “me”ti ca vuccamānassa atthassa ākārādibhūtassa dhammānaṃ asallakkhaṇabhāvato avijjamānapaññattibhāvoti āha “saccikaṭṭhaparamatthavasena avijjamānapaññattī”ti. Saccikaṭṭhaparamatthavasenāti [M 1.0155] ca bhūtatthauttamatthavasenāti attho. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – yo māyāmarīciādayo [V 1.0137] viya abhūtattho, anussavādīhi gahetabbo viya anuttamattho ca na hoti, so rūpasaddādisabhāvo, ruppanānubhavanādisabhāvo vā attho “saccikaṭṭho, paramattho”ti ca vuccati, “evaṃ me”ti padānaṃ pana attho abhūtattā, anuttamattā ca na tathā vuccati, tasmā bhūtatthauttamatthasaṅkhātena saccikaṭṭhaparamatthavasena visesanabhūtena avijjamānapaññattiyevāti. Etena ca visesanena bālajanehi “atthī”ti parikappitaṃ paññattimattaṃ nivatteti. Tadevatthaṃ pākaṭaṃ karoti, hetunā vā sādheti “kiñhettha ta”ntiādinā. Yaṃ dhammajātaṃ, atthajātaṃ vā “eva”nti vā “me”ti vā niddesaṃ labhetha, taṃ ettha rūpaphassādidhammasamudāye, “evaṃ me”ti padānaṃ vā atthe. Paramatthato na atthīti yojanā. Rūpaphassādibhāvena niddiṭṭho paramatthato ettha attheva, “evaṃ me”ti pana niddiṭṭho natthīti adhippāyo. Sutanti pana saddāyatanaṃ sandhāyāha “vijjamānapaññattī”ti. “Saccikaṭṭhaparamatthavasenā”ti cettha adhikāro. “Yañhī”tiādi tappākaṭīkaraṇaṃ, hetudassanaṃ vā. Yaṃ taṃ saddāyatanaṃ sotena sotadvārena, tannissitaviññāṇena vā upaladdhaṃ adhigamitabbanti attho. Tena hi saddāyatanamidha gahitaṃ kammasādhanenāti dasseti.

Because the meaning of everything knowable through words must be understood only through the portal of designation, and because all designations are included in the six kinds of designation by way of the existent, etc., the commentator, having determined the nature of the designations such as 'evaṃ' among them, wishing to show it, said the passage beginning 'evanti ca'. Therein, because the meaning—which is the mode, etc.—spoken of as 'evaṃ' and 'me' is not a markable characteristic of dhammas, it is a designation of the non-existent. Therefore, he said: 'a designation of the non-existent by way of ultimate reality in the true sense'. 'By way of ultimate reality in the true sense' means by way of a real meaning and a supreme meaning. This is what is meant: That meaning which is not an unreal meaning like an illusion or a mirage, and not a non-supreme meaning like that which is grasped through oral tradition, etc.—that meaning which has the nature of form, sound, etc., or has the nature of being afflicted, experiencing, etc., is called 'in the true sense' and 'ultimate'. However, the meaning of the words 'evaṃ me' is not so called because it is unreal and not supreme. Therefore, it is only a designation of the non-existent, qualified by 'by way of ultimate reality in the true sense', which is designated as a real and supreme meaning. And by this qualifier, he refutes the mere designation that is imagined by foolish people as 'it exists'. He makes that very meaning clear, or establishes it with a reason, with the passage beginning 'kiñhettha taṃ'. Whatever kind of phenomenon or kind of meaning might receive the designation 'evaṃ' or 'me', that does not exist in an ultimate sense here in this collection of dhammas such as form and contact, or in the meaning of the words 'evaṃ me'. This is the interpretation. The meaning indicated as the state of form, contact, etc., does indeed exist here in an ultimate sense. But the meaning indicated as 'evaṃ me' does not. This is the intention. However, with reference to the sound-base, he says of 'sutaṃ' that it is 'a designation of the existent'. And here, the phrase 'by way of ultimate reality in the true sense' is the governing phrase. The passage beginning 'Yañhi' is its clarification, or a showing of the reason. The meaning is: that sound-base is obtained or is to be known by the ear, the ear-door, or by the consciousness dependent on it. For by that word ['sutaṃ'], it is shown that the sound-base is here taken with the passive construction (kammasādhana).

Evaṃ aṭṭhakathānayena paññattisarūpaṃ niddhāretvā idāni aṭṭhakathāmuttakenāpi nayena vuttesu chasu paññattibhedesu “eva”ntiādīnaṃ paññattīnaṃ sarūpaṃ niddhārento “tathā”tiādimāha. Upādāpaññatti ādayo hi porāṇaṭṭhakathāto muttā saṅgahakāreneva ācariyena vuttā. Vitthāro abhidhammaṭṭhakathāya gahetabbo. Taṃ tanti taṃ taṃ dhammajātaṃ, sotapathamāgate dhamme upādāya tesaṃ upadhāritākāranidassanāvadhāraṇassa paccāmasanavasena evanti ca sasantatipariyāpanne khandhe upādāya meti ca vattabbattāti attho. Rūpavedanādibhedehi dhamme upādāya nissāya kāraṇaṃ katvā paññatti upādāpaññatti yathā “tāni tāni aṅgāni upādāya ratho gehaṃ, te te rūparasādayo upādāya ghaṭo paṭo, candimasūriyaparivattādayo upādāya kālo disā”tiādi. Paññapetabbaṭṭhena cesā paññatti nāma, na paññāpanaṭṭhena. Yā pana tassa atthassa paññāpanā, ayaṃ avijjamānapaññattiyeva. Diṭṭhādīni upanidhāya [M 1.0156] vattabbatoti diṭṭhamutaviññāte upanidhāya upatthambhaṃ katvā apekkhitvā vattabbattā. Diṭṭhādisabhāvavirahite saddāyatane vattamānopi hi sutavohāro “dutiyaṃ tatiya”ntiādiko viya paṭhamādīni diṭṭhamutaviññāte apekkhitvā pavatto “upanidhāpaññatī”ti vuccate. Sā panesā anekavidhā tadaññapekkhūpanidhā hatthagatūpanidhā sampayuttūpanidhāsamāropitūpanidhā avidūragatūpanidhā paṭibhāgūpanidhā tabbahulūpanidhātabbisiṭṭhūpanidhā”tiādinā. Tāsu ayaṃ “dutiyaṃ tatiya”ntiādikā viya paṭhamādīnaṃ diṭṭhādīnaṃ aññamaññamapekkhitvā vuttattā tadaññapekkhūpanidhāpaññatti nāma.

Thus, having determined the nature of designation according to the commentary method, now, wishing to determine the nature of designations such as 'evaṃ' among the six kinds of designations mentioned, also by a method independent of the commentary, the commentator states 'tathā' and so on. Indeed, dependent designation and so on, being independent of the ancient commentaries, were stated by the method of the teacher who was the author of the Saṅgaha. The detailed explanation should be taken from the Abhidhamma commentary on the Puggalapaññatti. 'That' and 'that' refers to that particular class of phenomena. The meaning is that 'evaṃ' (thus) is to be said by taking as a basis the phenomena that have come into the range of the ear-door, by way of repeatedly reflecting on the ascertained mode, indication, and determination of those phenomena; and 'me' (mine) is to be said by taking as a basis the aggregates included in one's own continuity. Taking as a basis, relying on, and making a cause of phenomena such as form, feeling, etc., the designation is called 'dependent designation' (upādāpaññatti), as in: 'Taking as a basis those various parts, [there is] a chariot, a house; taking as a basis those various forms, tastes, etc., [there is] a pot, a cloth; taking as a basis the revolutions of the moon and sun, etc., [there are] time and directions,' and so on. And this is called 'designation' (paññatti) in the sense of that which is to be made known, not in the sense of the act of making known. But the act of making that meaning known is indeed a 'non-existent designation' (avijjamānapaññatti). 'It is to be stated by placing near the seen, etc.' means because it is to be stated by placing near, making a support of, and depending on what is seen, heard, and cognized. Indeed, even though it occurs in the sound-base, which is devoid of the nature of the seen, etc., the conventional speech of 'heard' (sutavohāro), which proceeds in dependence on the first, etc., that are seen, heard, and cognized—like 'second,' 'third,' and so on—is called 'designation by placing near' (upanidhāpaññatti). Moreover, this is of many kinds: designation by reference to another, designation by possession, designation by association, designation by imputation, designation by non-distance, designation by counterpart, designation by abundance, designation by excellence, and so on. Among these, this one, like 'second, third,' etc., is called 'designation by reference to another' (tadaññapekkhūpanidhāpaññatti) because it is stated in mutual dependence on the first, etc., of the seen, etc.

Evaṃ paññattiyāpi [V 1.0138] atthādhigamanīyatāsaṅkhātaṃ dassetabbatthaṃ dassetvā idāni saddasāmatthiyena dīpetabbamatthaṃ niddhāretvā dīpento “ettha cā”tiādimāha. Etthāti etasmiṃ vacanattaye. Ca-saddo upanyāso atthantaraṃ ārabhitukāmena yojitattā. “Suta”nti vutte asutaṃ na hotīti pakāsitoyamattho, tasmā tathā suta-saddena pakāsitā attanā paṭividdhasuttassa pakāravisesā “eva”nti therena paccāmaṭṭhāti tena evaṃ-saddena asammoho dīpito nāma, tenāha “evanti vacanena asammohaṃ dīpetī”ti. Asammohanti ca yathāsute sutte asammohaṃ. Tadeva yuttiyā, byatirekena ca samatthehi “na hī”tiādinā vakkhamānañca suttaṃ nānappakāraṃ duppaṭividdhañca. Evaṃ nānappakāre duppaṭividdhe sutte kathaṃ sammūḷho nānappakārapaṭivedhasamattho bhavissati. Imāya yuttiyā, iminā ca byatirekena therassa tattha asammūḷhabhāvasaṅkhāto dīpetabbo attho viññāyatīti vuttaṃ hoti. Evamīdisesu yathārahaṃ. Bhagavato sammukhā sutākārassa yāthāvato upari therena dassiyamānattā “suttassa asammosaṃ dīpetī”ti vuttaṃ. Kālantarenāti sutakālato aparena kālena. Yassa…pe… paṭijānāti, therassa pana suvaṇṇabhājane pakkhittasīhavasā viya anassamānaṃ asammuṭṭhaṃ tiṭṭhati, tasmā so evaṃ paṭijānātīti vuttaṃ hoti. Evaṃ dīpitena pana atthena kiṃ pakāsitanti āha “iccassā”tiādi. Tattha iccassāti iti assa, tasmā asammohassa, asammosassa ca dīpitattā assa therassapaññāsiddhītiādinā sambandho. Asammohenāti sammohābhāvena. Paññāvajjitasamādhiādidhammajātena taṃsampayuttāya paññāya [M 1.0157] siddhi sahajātādisattiyā sijjhanato. Sammohapaṭipakkhena vā paññāsaṅkhātena dhammajātena. Savanakālasambhūtāya hi paññāya taduttarikālapaññāsiddhi upanissayādikoṭiyā sijjhanato. Itaratthāpi yathārahaṃ nayo netabbo.

In this way, having shown the meaning to be shown, which is called 'the attainability of the meaning,' even by designation, now, wishing to determine and illuminate the meaning to be illuminated by the power of the words, the commentator states 'ettha ca' and so on. 'Ettha' means in this triad of words. The word 'ca' is an introduction, because it is used by one who wishes to begin another topic. When 'sutaṃ' (heard) is said, this meaning is made clear: that it is not unheard. Therefore, the particular characteristics of the sutta penetrated by himself, which were indicated by the word 'sutaṃ' in that way, were reflected upon by the Elder with 'evaṃ'; thus, by that word 'evaṃ', non-confusion is illuminated. Therefore, he said, 'By the word "evaṃ", he illuminates non-confusion.' And 'non-confusion' means non-confusion regarding the sutta as it was heard. He supports that very point by reasoning and by contrast with 'na hi' and so on, stating that the sutta to be explained is of various kinds and difficult to penetrate. Thus, when the sutta is of various kinds and difficult to penetrate, how will a confused person be capable of penetrating its various aspects? By this reasoning and by this contrast, the meaning to be shown—namely, the Elder’s state of non-confusion in that matter—is understood; this is what is meant. Thus, in such cases, it should be understood as appropriate. Because the Elder will later show the true nature of the manner of hearing from the presence of the Blessed One, it is said, 'He illuminates non-forgetfulness regarding the sutta.' 'Kālantarena' means at a time other than the time of hearing. For whomever what was heard is forgotten, that person, after some time, does not admit, 'It was heard by me.' For the Elder, however, it remains undissipated and unforgotten, like lion's fat placed in a golden vessel; therefore, he admits thus; this is what is meant. Furthermore, by the meaning thus illuminated, what is made clear? In response, he says 'iccassa' and so on. Therein, 'iccassa' is 'iti assa'. Therefore, because non-confusion and non-forgetfulness have been illuminated, the connection is made with 'the accomplishment of wisdom for this Elder' and so on. 'Asammohena' means by the absence of confusion. The accomplishment of wisdom associated with that class of phenomena, such as concentration, etc., which is faultless, is due to its fulfillment through the power of co-nascence, etc. Or, by the class of phenomena designated as wisdom, which is the opponent of confusion. Indeed, for the wisdom that arose at the time of hearing, the accomplishment of subsequent wisdom is fulfilled by way of the highest degree of decisive support condition, etc. In other instances too, the method should be applied as appropriate.

Evaṃ pakāsitena pana atthena kiṃ vibhāvitanti āha “tatthā”tiādi. Tatthāti tesu dubbidhesu dhammesu. Byañjanānaṃ paṭivijjhitabbo ākāro nātigambhīro, yathāsutadhāraṇameva tattha karaṇīyaṃ, tasmā tattha satiyā byāpāro adhiko, paññā pana guṇībhūtāti vuttaṃ “paññāpubbaṅgamāyā”tiādi. Paññāya pubbaṅgamā paññāpubbaṅgamāti hi nibbacanaṃ, pubbaṅgamatā cettha padhānabhāvo “manopubbaṅgamā dhammā”tiādīsu (dha. pa. 1) viya. Apica yathā cakkhuviññāṇādīsu āvajjanādayo pubbaṅgamā samānāpi tadārammaṇassa avijānanato appadhānabhūtā, evaṃ pubbaṅgamāyapi appadhānatte sati paññāpubbaṅgamā etissāti nibbacanampi yujjati. Pubbaṅgamatā cettha purecāribhāvo. Iti sahajātapubbaṅgamo purejātapubbaṅgamoti duvidhopi pubbaṅgamo idha sambhavati, yathā cettha, evaṃ sati “pubbaṅgamāyā”ti etthāpi yathāsambhavamesa [V 1.0139] nayo veditabbo. Evaṃ vibhāvitena samatthatāvacanena kimanubhāvitanti āha “tadubhayasamatthatāyogenā”tiādi. Tattha atthabyañjanasampannassāti atthabyañjanena paripuṇṇassa, saṅkāsanādīhi vā chahi atthapadehi, akkharādīhi ca chahi byañjanapadehi samannāgatassa, atthabyañjanasaṅkhātena vā rasena sādurasassa. Pariyattidhammoyeva navalokuttararatanasannidhānato sattavidhassa, dasavidhassa vā ratanassa sannidhāno koso viyāti dhammakoso, tathā dhammabhaṇḍāgāro, tattha niyuttoti dhammabhaṇḍāgāriko. Atha vā nānārājabhaṇḍarakkhako bhaṇḍāgāriko viyāti bhaṇḍāgāriko, dhammassa anurakkhako bhaṇḍāgārikoti tameva sadisatākāraṇadassanena visesetvā “dhammabhaṇḍāgāriko”ti vutto. Yathāha –

Since it may be asked, 'Furthermore, what is elucidated by the meaning thus explained?', the author states, 'tatthā,' and so on. ‘Tattha’ means: among those twofold states, namely mindfulness and wisdom. The mode of penetrating the expressions is not too profound; what is to be done there is simply to retain what has been heard. Therefore, in that regard, the function of mindfulness is greater, while wisdom becomes secondary. Thus it was said, 'preceded by wisdom,' and so on. Indeed, the explanation is: 'that which has wisdom as its forerunner is paññāpubbaṅgamā.' And here, 'being a forerunner' means being primary, as in 'Mind is the forerunner of all things,' and so on. Moreover, just as in eye-consciousness and so on, although adverting and so on are forerunners, they become non-primary because they do not cognize that object, so too, even when wisdom is a forerunner, when there is a state of non-primacy, the derivation 'for this (mindfulness), wisdom is the forerunner' is also suitable. And here, 'being a forerunner' means 'going before.' Thus, both kinds of forerunner—the co-arisen forerunner and the pre-arisen forerunner—are possible here. And just as here, so too in the case of 'preceded by mindfulness,' this same method should be understood according to what is possible. Since it may be asked, 'By the statement of capability thus elucidated, what is indicated?', the author states, 'By the conjunction of the capability for both,' and so on. Therein, 'endowed with meaning and expression' means complete with meaning and expression; or possessed of the six terms of meaning beginning with indication, and the six terms of expression beginning with letters; or of excellent taste through the flavor called meaning and expression. The scriptural Dhamma itself, because it is a repository for the nine supramundane jewels, is like a treasury that is a repository for the sevenfold or tenfold jewel; therefore, it is the 'Dhamma-treasury,' and likewise the 'Dhamma-storehouse.' One appointed to that is a 'Dhamma-treasurer.' Alternatively, like a treasurer who guards the various royal treasures, so he is a 'treasurer.' A treasurer is a guardian of the Dhamma. Therefore, by showing the reason for this similarity, he is specified and called a 'Dhamma-treasurer.' As it was said:

“Bahussuto dhammadharo, sabbapāṭhī ca sāsane;

Ānando nāma nāmena, dhammārakkho tavaṃ mune”ti. (apa. 1.542);

“Learned, a bearer of the Dhamma, and one who knows all recitations in the Dispensation; Ānanda by name—you are a guardian of the Dhamma, O Sage!”

Aññathāpi dīpetabbamatthaṃ dīpeti “aparo nayo”tiādinā, evaṃ saddena vuccamānānaṃ ākāranidassanāvadhāraṇatthānaṃ aviparītasaddhammavisayattā tabbisayehi [M 1.0158] tehi atthehi yoniso manasikārassa dīpanaṃ yuttanti vuttaṃ “yoni…pe… dīpetī”ti. “Ayoniso”tiādinā byatirekena ñāpakahetudassanaṃ. Tattha katthaci hi-saddo dissati, so kāraṇe, kasmāti attho, iminā vacaneneva yoniso manasikaroto nānappakārapaṭivedhasambhavato aggi viya dhūmena kāriyena kāraṇabhūto so viññāyatīti tadanvayampi atthāpattiyā dasseti. Esa nayo sabbattha yathārahaṃ. “Brahmajālaṃ āvuso kattha bhāsita”ntiādi pucchāvasena adhunā pakaraṇappattassa vakkhamānassa suttassa “suta”nti padena vuccamānaṃ bhagavato sammukhā savanaṃ samādhānamantarena na sambhavatīti katvā vuttaṃ “avikkhepaṃ dīpetī”ti. “Vikkhittacittassā”tiādinā byatirekakāraṇena ñāpakahetuṃ dassetvā tadeva samattheti “tathā hī”tiādinā. Sabbasampattiyāti sabbena atthabyañjanadesakapayojanādinā sampattiyā. Kiṃ iminā pakāsitanti āha “yoniso manasikārena cetthā”tiādi. Etthāti etasmiṃ dhammadvaye. “Na hi vikkhittacitto”tiādinā kāraṇabhūtena avikkhepena, sappurisūpanissayena ca phalabhūtassa saddhammassavanassa siddhiyā eva samatthanaṃ vuttaṃ, avikkhepena pana sappurisūpanissayassa siddhiyā samatthanaṃ na vuttaṃ. Kasmāti ce? Vikkhittacittānaṃ sappurise payirupāsanābhāvassa atthato siddhattā. Atthavaseneva hi so pākaṭoti na vutto.

The author illuminates the meaning to be illuminated in another way with 'another method,' and so on. Because the meanings of mode, example, and determination, which are expressed by the word 'evaṃ' (thus), have the unperverted true Dhamma as their domain, it is fitting to illuminate wise attention by means of those meanings within that domain; thus it was said, 'wisely... illuminates.' With 'unwisely,' and so on, the indicative cause is shown by way of the negative. Therein, the word 'hi' is sometimes seen; it is in the sense of cause, meaning 'why?'. By this very statement, because for one who applies wise attention there is the possibility of various kinds of penetration, just as fire, the cause, is known by smoke, the effect, so is that wise attention, the cause, known by the various kinds of penetration, the effect. Therefore, he also shows its positive concomitance by implication. This method is to be understood everywhere as appropriate. By way of the question, 'Friend, where was the Brahmajāla Sutta spoken?' and so on, regarding the discourse now relevant to the context, the hearing directly from the Blessed One which is expressed by the word 'sutaṃ' (heard) is not possible without concentration. For this reason, it was said, 'he illuminates non-distraction.' Having shown the indicative cause by way of the negative cause with 'of one with a distracted mind,' and so on, he supports that very point with 'tathā hi' (for thus), and so on. 'With all accomplishment' means with the full accomplishment of meaning, expression, teacher, purpose, and so on. Since it may be asked, 'What is explained by this?', the author states, 'yoniso manasikārena cettha,' and so on. 'Ettha' (herein) means: in this pair of states. With 'na hi vikkhittacitto' (for one with a distracted mind...), and so on, the establishment of the accomplishment of hearing the true Dhamma, which is the fruit, is stated only by means of non-distraction and association with a good person, which are the causes. However, the establishment of the accomplishment of association with a good person by means of non-distraction is not stated. Why? Because for those with distracted minds, the absence of associating with good people is established by the meaning itself. Indeed, that meaning is evident by the force of the meaning, so it is not stated.

Etthāha – yathā yoniso manasikārena phalabhūtena attasammāpaṇidhipubbekatapuññatānaṃ kāraṇabhūtānaṃ [V 1.0140] siddhi vuttā tadavinābhāvato, evaṃ avikkhepena phalabhūtena saddhammassavanasappurisūpanissayānaṃ kāraṇabhūtānaṃ siddhi vattabbā siyā assutavato, sappurisūpanissayavirahitassa ca tadabhāvato. Evaṃ santepi “na hi vikkhittacitto”tiādisamatthanavacanena avikkhepena, sappurisūpanissayena ca kāraṇabhūtena saddhammassavanasseva phalabhūtassa siddhi vuttā, kasmā panevaṃ vuttāti? Vuccate – adhippāyantarasambhavato hi tathā siddhi vuttā. Ayaṃ panetthādhippāyo – saddhammassavanasappurisūpanissayā na ekantena avikkhepassa kāraṇaṃ bāhirakāraṇattā, avikkhepo pana sappurisūpanissayo viya saddhammassavanassa ekantakāraṇaṃ ajjhattikakāraṇattā, tasmā ekantakāraṇe honte kimatthiyā anekantakāraṇaṃ pati phalabhāvaparikappanāti tathāyevetassa [M 1.0159] siddhi vuttāti. Ettha ca paṭhamaṃ phalena kāraṇassa siddhidassanaṃ nadīpūrena viya upari vuṭṭhisabbhāvassa, dutiyaṃ kāraṇena phalassa siddhidassanaṃ ekantavassinā viya meghavuṭṭhānena vuṭṭhipavattiyā.

Here an objection is raised: Just as the accomplishment of right self-aspiration and the state of having past merit, which are the causes, is stated by means of wise attention, which is the fruit, due to their inseparability; so too, the accomplishment of hearing the true Dhamma and association with good persons, which are the causes, should be stated by means of non-distraction, which is the fruit, because for one who has not heard and for one devoid of association with good persons, that (non-distraction) is absent. Even though this is so, with the supporting statement 'for indeed, one with a distracted mind,' and so on, the accomplishment of only hearing the true Dhamma, which is the fruit, is stated by means of non-distraction and association with a good person, which are the causes. But why is it stated thus? It is said: Indeed, the accomplishment is stated thus because of the possibility of a different intention. And this is the intention here: Hearing the true Dhamma and association with good persons are not the invariable cause of non-distraction, because they are external causes. Non-distraction, however, like association with good persons, is the invariable cause of hearing the true Dhamma, because it is an internal cause. Therefore, when there is an invariable cause, for what purpose is there the conceiving of a fruit-state in relation to a non-invariable cause? Thus its accomplishment is stated in just that way. And here, the first is the showing of the cause's accomplishment by the fruit, like the showing of the existence of rain upstream by the flooding of the river. The second is the showing of the fruit's accomplishment by the cause, like the showing of the occurrence of rain by the rising of a cloud that will invariably rain.

“Aparo nayo”tiādinā aññathāpi dīpetabbatthamāha, yasmā na hotīti sambandho. Evanti…pe… nānākāraniddesoti heṭṭhā vuttaṃ, so ca ākāroti sotadvārānusāraviññāṇavīthisaṅkhātassa cittasantānassa nānākārena ārammaṇe pavattiyā nānatthabyañjanaggahaṇasaṅkhāto so bhagavato vacanassa atthabyañjanappabhedaparicchedavasena sakalasāsanasampattiogāhanākāro. Evaṃ bhaddakoti niravasesaparahitapāripūribhāvakāraṇattā evaṃ yathāvuttena nānatthabyañjanaggahaṇena sundaro seṭṭho, samāsapadaṃ vā etaṃ evaṃ īdiso bhaddo yassāti katvā. Na paṇihito appaṇihito, sammā appaṇi hito attā yassāti tathā, tassa. Pacchimacakkadvayasampattinti attasammāpaṇidhipubbekatapuññatāsaṅkhātaguṇadvayasampattiṃ. Guṇasseva hi aparāparavuttiyā pavattanaṭṭhena cakkabhāvo. Caranti vā etena sattā sampattibhavaṃ, sampattibhavesūti vā cakkaṃ. Yaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “cattārimāni bhikkhave, cakkāni, yehi samannāgatānaṃ devamanussānaṃ catucakkaṃ vattatī”tiādi (a. ni. 4.31) pacchimabhāvo cettha desanākkamavaseneva. Purimacakkadvayasampattinti patirūpadesavāsasappurisūpanissayasaṅkhātaguṇadvayasampattiṃ. Sesaṃ vuttanayameva. Tasmāti purimakāraṇaṃ purimassevāti idha kāraṇamāha “na hī”tiādinā.

With “Another method,” and so on, he states the meaning to be explained in another way. The connection “because it is not” should be made. As for “Thus… the exposition of various aspects,” which was stated below, that manner is called the grasping of various meanings and expressions through the occurrence in various ways towards an object of the mind-continuum, which is known as the consciousness-process that proceeds in sequence to the ear-door. That is the manner of entering into the perfection of the entire Dispensation by means of distinguishing the divisions of meaning and expression of the Blessed One's word. “Thus excellent” (evaṃ bhaddako) means that because it is the cause for the complete fulfillment of others' welfare without remainder, it is beautiful and excellent by means of the grasping of various meanings and expressions as stated. Or, this is a compound word, formed as: “that for which there is such an excellence.” Not directed is “undirected” (appaṇihito); one whose mind (attā) is rightly undirected is so-called. For that one, “the accomplishment of the two later wheels” means the accomplishment of the pair of qualities called right self-direction and the state of having done meritorious deeds in the past. Indeed, the state of being a wheel is due to the meaning of proceeding by the successive occurrence of the quality itself. Or, by this, beings proceed to a state of accomplishment; or, because they proceed in states of accomplishment, it is a wheel. Referring to which it was said: “Monks, there are these four wheels. For gods and humans who are endowed with them, the fourfold wheel turns,” and so on. And here, the state of being “later” is simply by way of the sequence of the discourse. “The accomplishment of the two former wheels” means the accomplishment of the pair of qualities called dwelling in a suitable region and resorting to good persons. The rest is just as has been stated. By “Therefore” (tasmā), the former cause is stated. Here, for “of the former itself” (purimasseva), he states the cause with “for it is not” (na hi), and so on.

Tena kiṃ pakāsitanti āha “iccassā”tiādi. Iti imāya catucakkasampattiyā kāraṇabhūtāya. Assa therassa. Pacchimacakkadvayasiddhiyāti pacchimacakkadvayassa atthibhāvena siddhiyā[V 1.0141]. Āsayasuddhīti vipassanāñāṇasaṅkhātāya anulomikakhantiyā, kammassakatāñāṇa-maggañāṇasaṅkhātassa yathābhūtañāṇassa cāti duvidhassāpi āsayassa asuddhihetubhūtānaṃ kilesānaṃ dūrībhāvena suddhi. Tadeva hi dvayaṃ vivaṭṭanissitānaṃ suddhasattānaṃ āsayo. Sammāpaṇihitatto hi pubbe ca katapuñño suddhāsayo hoti. Tathā hi vuttaṃ “sammāpaṇihitaṃ cittaṃ, seyyaso naṃ tato kare”ti, (dha. pa. 43) “katapuññosi tvaṃ ānanda, padhānamanuyuñja [M 1.0160] khippaṃ hohisi anāsavo”ti (dī. ni. 2.207) ca. Keci pana “kattukamyatāchando āsayo”ti vadanti, tadayuttameva “tāya ca āsayasuddhiyā adhigamabyattisiddhī”ti vacanena virodhato. Evampi maggañāṇasaṅkhātassa āsayassa suddhi na yuttā tāya adhigamabyattisiddhiyā avattabbatoti? No na yutto purimassa maggassa, pacchimānaṃ maggānaṃ, phalānañca kāraṇabhāvato. Payogasuddhīti yonisomanasikārapubbaṅgamassa dhammassavanapayogassa visadabhāvena suddhi, sabbassa vā kāyavacīpayogassa niddosabhāvena suddhi. Patirūpadesavāsī, hi sappurisasevī ca yathāvuttavisuddhapayogo hoti. Tathāvisuddhena yonisomanasikārapubbaṅgamena dhammassavanapayogena, vippaṭisārābhāvāvahena ca kāyavacīpayogena avikkhittacitto pariyattiyaṃ visārado hoti, tathābhūto ca thero, tena viññāyati purimacakkadvayasiddhiyā therassa payogasuddhi siddhāvāti. Tena kiṃ vibhāvitanti āha “tāya cā”tiādi. Adhigamabyattisiddhīti paṭivedhasaṅkhāte adhigame chekabhāvasiddhi. Adhigametabbato hi paṭivijjhitabbato paṭivedho “adhigamo”ti aṭṭhakathāsu vutto, āgamoti ca pariyatti āgacchanti attatthaparatthādayo etena, ābhuso vā gamitabbo ñātabboti katvā.

Because it should be asked, “What is explained by that?”, he says “iccassā,” and so on. Thus, for this Elder, by this accomplishment of the four wheels which is the cause. “By the success of the two later wheels” means by the success due to the existence of the two later wheels. “Purity of disposition” (āsayasuddhi) means purity through the removal of the defilements that are the cause of impurity for both kinds of disposition: namely, conformity tolerance, which is called insight-knowledge, and the knowledge of things as they really are, which is called the knowledge of ownership of kamma and path-knowledge. Indeed, that very pair is the disposition of pure beings who rely on that which is free from the round of rebirth. For one with a rightly directed mind and who has done meritorious deeds in the past has a pure disposition. For so it was said: “A rightly directed mind can do for one what is more excellent than that,” and “You, Ānanda, have made merit; apply yourself to the endeavor, and you will soon be without taints.” But some say, “Disposition is the wholesome desire which is the wish to do.” That is unsuitable because it contradicts the statement, “And by that purity of disposition, there is the success of proficiency in realization.” Even so, is the purity of the disposition called path-knowledge not suitable, because by that the success of proficiency in realization is not to be spoken of? No, it is not unsuitable, because the former path is the cause for the later paths and fruits. “Purity of effort” (payogasuddhi) means purity through the clarity of the effort of listening to the Dhamma, which is preceded by wise attention; or, purity through the faultlessness of all bodily and verbal effort. Indeed, one who dwells in a suitable place and associates with good persons has the aforesaid pure effort. With such pure effort of listening to the Dhamma, which is preceded by wise attention, and with bodily and verbal effort that brings about an absence of remorse, one becomes undistracted in mind and proficient in the scriptures. And the Elder was such a one. Therefore, it is understood that the Elder's purity of effort was accomplished through the success of the two former wheels. Because it should be asked, “What is clarified by that?”, he says “tāya ca,” and so on. “Success of proficiency in realization” (adhigamabyattisiddhi) means the accomplishment of skill in realization, which is called penetration. For penetration (paṭivedha) is called “realization” (adhigama) in the commentaries because it is to be realized and to be penetrated. And “scripture” (āgama) means the scriptural tradition (pariyatti). It is so called because one's own welfare, the welfare of others, and so on, are arrived at (āgacchanti) by means of it; or because it is to be gone to (gamitabbo) or known (ñātabbo) exceedingly (ābhuso).

Tena kimanubhāvitanti āha “itī”tiādi. Itīti evaṃ vuttanayena, tasmā siddhattāti vā kāraṇaniddeso. Vacananti nidānavacanaṃ lokato, dhammato ca siddhāya upamāya tamatthaṃ ñāpetuṃ “aruṇuggaṃ viyā”tiādimāha. “Upamāya midhekacce, atthaṃ jānanti paṇḍitā”ti (jā. 2.19.24) hi vuttaṃ. Aruṇoti sūriyassa udayato pubbabhāge uṭṭhitaraṃsi, tassa uggaṃ uggamanaṃ udayato udayantassa udayāvāsamuggacchato sūriyassa pubbaṅgamaṃ purecaraṃ bhavituṃ arahati viyāti sambandho. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – āgamādhigamabyattiyā īdisassa therassa vuttanidānavacanaṃ bhagavato vacanassa pubbaṅgamaṃ bhavitumarahati, nidānabhāvaṃ gataṃ hotīti idamatthajātaṃ anubhāvitanti.

Because it should be asked, “What is made evident by that?”, he says “iti,” and so on. “Iti” is an indication of the cause, meaning “in the manner thus stated,” or “therefore, because it is accomplished.” As for “the statement” (vacanaṃ), it is the introductory statement. In order to make that meaning known by a simile established both from the world and from the Dhamma, he says “like the rising of the dawn,” and so on. For it was said: “Here, some wise people understand the meaning by a simile.” “Dawn” (aruṇa) is the light that has arisen in the period before the sun rises from the east. The connection should be made thus: just as its rising is fit to be the forerunner, the precursor, of the sun rising from the east. This is what is meant: the introductory statement spoken by such an Elder, who is proficient in the scriptures and in realization, is fit to be the forerunner of the Blessed One's word; it has come to be the introduction. Thus, this nature of meaning is made evident.

Idāni aparampi pubbe vuttassa asammohāsammosasaṅkhātassa dīpetabbassatthassa dīpakehi evaṃ-sadda suta-saddehi pakāsetabbamatthaṃ pakāsento “aparo nayo”tiādimāha. Tattha hi “nānappakārapaṭivedhadīpakena[V 1.0142], sotabbappabhedapaṭivedhadīpakenā”ti ca iminā tehi saddehi pubbe [M 1.0161] dīpitaṃ asammohāsammosasaṅkhātaṃ dīpetabbatthamāha asammohena nānappakārapaṭivedhassa, asammosena ca sotabbappabhedapaṭivedhassa sijjhanato. “Attano”tiādīhi pana pakāsetabbatthaṃ. Tena vuttaṃ ācariyadhammapālattherena “nānappakārapaṭivedhadīpakenātiādinā evaṃ-sadda suta-saddānaṃ therassa atthabyañjanesu asammohāsammosadīpanato catupaṭisambhidāvasena atthayojanaṃ dassetī”ti (dī. ni. ṭī. 1.1). Hetugabbhañcetaṃ padadvayaṃ, nānappakārapaṭivedhasaṅkhātassa, sotabbappabheda-paṭivedhasaṅkhātassa ca dīpetabbatthassa dīpakattāti vuttaṃ hoti. Santassa vijjamānassa bhāvo sabbhāvo, atthapaṭibhānapaṭisambhidāhi sampattiyā sabbhāvo tathā. “Sambhava”ntipi pāṭho, sambhavanaṃ sambhavo, atthapaṭibhānapaṭisambhidāsampattīnaṃ sambhavo tathā. Evaṃ itaratthāpi. “Sotabbappabhedapaṭivedhadīpakenā”ti etena pana ayaṃ suta-saddo evaṃ-saddasannidhānato, vakkhamānāpekkhāya vā sāmaññeneva vuttepi sotabbadhammavisesaṃ āmasatīti dasseti. Ettha ca sotabbadhammasaṅkhātāya pāḷiyā nidassetabbānaṃ bhāsitatthapayojanatthānaṃ, tīsu ca ñāṇesu pavattañāṇassa nānappakārabhāvato tabbhāvapaṭivedhadīpakena evaṃ-saddena atthapaṭibhānapaṭisambhidāsampattisabbhāvadīpanaṃ yuttaṃ, sotabbadhammassa pana atthādhigamahetuto, taṃvasena ca tadavasesahetuppabhedassa gahitattā, niruttibhāvato ca sotabbappabhedadīpakena suta-saddena dhammaniruttipaṭisambhidāsampattisabbhāvadīpanaṃ yuttanti veditabbaṃ. Tadevatthañhi ñāpetuṃ “asammohadīpakena, asammosadīpakenā”ti ca avatvā tathā vuttanti.

Now, also clarifying another meaning to be explained—which was previously stated as that designated as non-delusion and non-forgetfulness—by means of the illuminators, the words 'evaṃ' and 'suta', the commentator, wishing to clarify the meaning to be expressed, says, 'aparo nayo' ('another method'), and so on. Therein, indeed, with the phrases 'by that which illuminates the penetration of various aspects' and 'by that which illuminates the penetration of the distinctions of what is to be heard,' he states the meaning to be explained, which was previously illuminated by those words as that designated as non-delusion and non-forgetfulness. This is because the penetration of various aspects is accomplished through non-delusion, and the penetration of the distinctions of what is to be heard is accomplished through non-forgetfulness. However, [he explains] the meaning to be expressed with 'attano' ('of oneself'), and so on. Therefore, it was said by the Elder Ācariya Dhammapāla: 'By the phrase beginning with "by that which illuminates the penetration of various aspects," he shows the application of the meaning by way of the four analytical knowledges, because the words 'evaṃ' and 'suta' illuminate the Elder's non-delusion and non-forgetfulness in the meaning and expression.' This pair of terms is pregnant with a cause, for it is said that they are illuminators of the meaning to be explained, which is designated as the penetration of various aspects and the penetration of the distinctions of what is to be heard. The state of being truly existent (sabbhāvo) is the state of what is present; such is the state of being truly existent of the attainment of the analytical knowledges of meaning (attha-paṭisambhidā) and ready wit (paṭibhāna-paṭisambhidā). There is also the reading 'sambhava' (arising); arising is 'sambhava'; such is the arising of the attainments of the analytical knowledges of meaning and ready wit. So too in the other case. However, by this phrase 'by that which illuminates the penetration of the distinctions of what is to be heard,' he shows that this word 'suta', due to its proximity to the word 'evaṃ' or in anticipation of what will be said, refers to the special qualities of the Dhamma to be heard, even when stated generally. And here, concerning the Pāli designated as the Dhamma to be heard, of the meanings of what is spoken and the meanings of its purpose, and of the knowledge that occurs in the three [other] analytical knowledges, because of its diverse nature, it is appropriate to illuminate the state of being truly existent of the attainment of the analytical knowledges of meaning and ready wit by the word 'evaṃ', as that which illuminates the penetration of that diverse nature. However, because the Dhamma to be heard is a cause for understanding the meaning, and because, by means of it, the distinctions of the remaining causes are grasped, and because of its nature as language (nirutti), it should be understood that it is appropriate to illuminate the state of being truly existent of the attainment of the analytical knowledges of Dhamma (dhamma-paṭisambhidā) and language (nirutti-paṭisambhidā) by the word 'suta', as that which illuminates the distinctions of what is to be heard. Indeed, to make known that very meaning, instead of saying 'by that which illuminates non-delusion' and 'by that which illuminates non-forgetfulness,' it was stated thus.

Evaṃ asammohāsammosasaṅkhātassa dīpetabbassatthassa dīpakehi evaṃ-sadda suta-saddehi pakāsetabbamatthaṃ pakāsetvā idāni yonisomanasikārāvikkhepasaṅkhātassa dīpetabbassatthassa dīpakehipi tehi pakāsetabbamatthaṃ pakāsento “evanti cā”tiādimāha. Tattha hi “evanti…pe… bhāsamāno, sutanti idaṃ…pe… bhāsamāno”ti ca iminā tehi saddehi pubbe dīpitaṃ yonisomanasikārāvikkhepasaṅkhātaṃ dīpetabbatthamāha, “ete mayā”tiādīhi pana pakāsetabbatthaṃ savanayogadīpakanti ca avikkhepavasena savanayogassa sijjhanato tadeva sandhāyāha[M 1.0162]. Tathā hi ācariyadhammapālattherena vuttaṃ “savanadhāraṇavacīparicariyā pariyattidhammānaṃ visesena sotāvadhāraṇapaṭibaddhāti te avikkhepadīpakena sutasaddena yojetvā”ti (dī. ni. ṭī. 1.1). Manodiṭṭhīhi pariyattidhammānaṃ anupekkhanasuppaṭivedhā visesato manasikārapaṭibaddhā, tasmā taddīpakavacaneneva ete mayā dhammā manasānupekkhitā diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhāti imamatthaṃ pakāsetīti vuttaṃ “evanti ca…pe… dīpetī”ti tattha dhammāti pariyattidhammā. Manasānupekkhitāti “idha sīlaṃ kathitaṃ, idha samādhi, idha paññā, ettakāva ettha [V 1.0143] anusandhayo”tiādibhedena manasā anupekkhitā. Diṭṭhiyā suppaṭividdhāti nijjhānakkhantisaṅkhātāya, ñātapariññāsaṅkhātāya vā diṭṭhiyā tattha vuttarūpārūpadhamme “iti rūpaṃ, ettakaṃ rūpa”ntiādinā suṭṭhu vavatthāpetvā paṭividdhā.

Having thus clarified the meaning to be expressed, designated as non-delusion and non-forgetfulness, by means of the illuminators, the words 'evaṃ' and 'suta', now, wishing to clarify the meaning to be expressed, designated as wise attention and non-distraction, also by means of those illuminators, the commentator says, 'evanti ca' ('And thus...'), and so on. Therein, indeed, with the phrases 'evanti...pe... bhāsamāno' ('Thus... speaking') and 'sutanti idaṃ...pe... bhāsamāno' ('This... heard... speaking'), he states the meaning to be explained, previously illuminated as that designated as wise attention and non-distraction. However, with 'ete mayā' ('these by me'), and so on, he states the meaning to be expressed. And the statement 'illuminating the application to hearing' is said with reference to that very non-distraction, because the application to hearing is accomplished by way of non-distraction. For so it was said by the Elder Ācariya Dhammapāla: 'The acts of hearing, retaining, and verbal practice of the textual Dhamma are especially connected with hearing and retaining; therefore, one should connect them with the word 'suta', which illuminates non-distraction.' The repeated contemplation and thorough penetration of the textual Dhamma by mind and wisdom are especially connected with attention. Therefore, by the very word that illuminates that, he clarifies this meaning: 'These Dhammas have been repeatedly contemplated by me with the mind and thoroughly penetrated with wisdom.' Thus it was said, 'evanti ca...pe... dīpeti' ('And thus... he illuminates'). Therein, 'dhammā' means the textual Dhamma. 'Repeatedly contemplated by mind' means repeatedly contemplated by mind in its various aspects, such as: 'Herein, virtue is taught; herein, concentration is taught; herein, wisdom is taught; just so many are the connections herein.' 'Thoroughly penetrated with wisdom' means that the material and immaterial phenomena taught therein have been penetrated, having been well defined as 'This is material form; this much is material form,' and so on, by the wisdom designated as reflective acceptance or by the wisdom designated as full understanding of the known.

Savanadhāraṇavacīparicariyā ca pariyattidhammānaṃ visesena sotāvadhāraṇapaṭibaddhā, tasmā taddīpakavacaneneva bahū mayā dhammā sutā dhātā vacasā paricitāti imamatthaṃ pakāsetīti vuttaṃ “sutanti idaṃ…pe… dīpetī”ti. Tattha sutāti sotadvārānusārena viññātā. Dhātāti suvaṇṇabhājane pakkhittasīhavasā viya manasi suppatiṭṭhitabhāvasādhanena upadhāritā. Vacasā paricitāti paguṇatāsampādanena vācāya paricitā sajjhāyitā. Idāni pakāsetabbatthadvayadīpakena yathāvuttasaddadvayena vibhāvetabbamatthaṃ vibhāvento “tadubhayenapī”tiādimāha. Tattha tadubhayenāti purimanaye, pacchimanaye ca yathāvuttassa pakāsetabbassatthassa pakāsakena tena dubbidhena saddena. Atthabyañjanapāripūriṃ dīpentoti ādarajananassa kāraṇavacanaṃ. Tadeva kāraṇaṃ byatirekena vivarati, yuttiyā vā daḷhaṃ karoti “atthabyañjanaparipuṇṇañhī”tiādinā. Asuṇantoti cettha lakkhaṇe, hetumhi vā anta-saddo. Mahatā hitāti mahantato hitasmā. Paribāhiroti sabbato bhāgena bāhiro.

The acts of hearing, retaining, and verbal practice are, in respect to the textual Dhamma, especially connected with hearing and retaining. Therefore, by the very word that illuminates that, he clarifies this meaning: 'Many Dhammas have been heard by me, retained, and made familiar by speech.' Thus it was said, 'sutanti idaṃ…pe… dīpetīti' ('This... heard... he illuminates'). Therein, 'sutā' (heard) means known in accordance with the ear-door. 'Dhātā' (retained) means borne in mind by accomplishing the state of being well-established in the mind, like lion's fat placed in a golden vessel. 'Vacasā paricitā' (made familiar by speech) means practiced with the voice, recited, by means of accomplishing proficiency. Now, clarifying the meaning to be made clear by the aforementioned pair of words that illuminates the twofold meaning to be expressed, the commentator says, 'tadubhayenapī' ('By both...'), and so on. Therein, 'tadubhayena' ('by both') refers to that twofold word which, in both the former and the latter methods, clarifies the meaning to be expressed as stated. The phrase 'showing the completeness of meaning and phrasing' is a statement of the cause for generating reverence. He explains that very cause by way of contrast, or strengthens it by reasoning, with the phrase beginning 'atthabyañjanaparipuṇṇañhī' ('For it is complete in meaning and phrasing'). In 'asuṇanto' ('not hearing'), the suffix '-anta' is in the sense of a characteristic or in the sense of a cause. 'Mahatā hitā' ('from great benefit') means from much benefit. 'Paribāhiro' ('excluded') means external in every respect.

Etena pana vibhāvetabbatthadīpakena saddadvayena anubhāvetabbatthamanubhāvento “evaṃ me sutanti iminā”tiādimāha. Pubbe visuṃ visuṃ atthe yojitāyeva ete saddā idha ekassevānubhāvatthassa anubhāvakabhāvena gahitāti ñāpetuṃ “sakalenā”ti vuttaṃ. Kāmañca me-saddo imasmiṃ [M 1.0163] ṭhāne pubbena yojito, tadapekkhānaṃ pana evaṃ-sadda suta-saddānaṃ sahacaraṇato, avinābhāvato ca tathā vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tathāgatappaveditanti tathāgatena pakārato viditaṃ, bhāsitaṃ vā. Attano adahantoti attani “mameda”nti aṭṭhapento. Bhummatthe cetaṃ sāmivacanaṃ. Asappurisabhūminti asappurisavisayaṃ, so ca atthato apakataññutāsaṅkhātā “idhekacco pāpabhikkhu tathāgatappaveditaṃ dhammavinayaṃ pariyāpuṇitvā attano dahatī”ti (pārā. 195) evaṃ mahācoradīpakena bhagavatā vuttā anariyavohārāvatthā, tathā cāha “tathāgata…pe… adahanto”ti. Hutvāti cettha seso. Tathā sāvakattaṃ paṭijānantoti sappurisabhūmiokkamanasarūpakathanaṃ.
