Tathā puttadārādikassa tividhassāpi hetu avītikkamanavasena tisso sīlapāramiyo, tesu eva tividhesu vatthūsu ālayaṃ upacchinditvā nikkhamanavasena tisso nekkhammapāramiyo, upakaraṇaaṅgajīvitataṇhaṃ samūhanitvā sattānaṃ hitāhitavinicchayakaraṇavasena tisso paññāpāramiyo, yathāvuttabhedānaṃ pariccāgādīnaṃ vāyamanavasena tisso vīriyapāramiyo, upakaraṇaaṅgajīvitantarāyakarānaṃ khamanavasena tisso khantipāramiyo, upakaraṇaaṅgajīvitahetu saccāpariccāgavasena tisso saccapāramiyo, dānādipāramiyo akuppādhiṭṭhānavaseneva samijjhantīti upakaraṇādivināsepi acalādhiṭṭhānavasena tisso adhiṭṭhānapāramiyo, upakaraṇādivighātakesupi sattesu mettāya avijahanavasena tisso mettāpāramiyo, yathāvuttavatthuttayassa upakārāpakāresu sattasaṅkhāresu majjhattatāpaṭilābhavasena tisso upekkhāpāramiyoti evamādinā etāsaṃ vibhāgo veditabbo.

Furthermore, the relinquishment of possessions such as children, spouse, and wealth is the perfection of giving; the relinquishment of one’s own limbs is the higher perfection of giving; the relinquishment of one’s own life is the ultimate perfection of giving. Likewise, by way of non-transgression on account of the threefold objects such as children, spouse, and so forth, there are the three perfections of virtue. In those same threefold objects, by way of going forth, having cut off attachment, there are the three perfections of renunciation. By uprooting craving for possessions, limbs, and life, and by way of discerning what is beneficial and not beneficial for beings, there are the three perfections of wisdom. By way of striving in the relinquishments and so forth of the kinds mentioned, there are the three perfections of energy. By way of enduring those who cause obstacles to possessions, limbs, and life, there are the three perfections of patience. By not abandoning truth for the sake of possessions, limbs, or life, there are the three perfections of truthfulness. Since the perfections of giving and others are accomplished only by way of an unshakeable resolution, even when possessions and the like are destroyed, by way of an unshakeable resolution, there are the three perfections of determination. By way of not abandoning loving-kindness toward beings who destroy possessions and the like, there are the three perfections of loving-kindness. By way of attaining a state of equanimity towards conditioned beings, whether they are helpful or unhelpful, with respect to the aforementioned threefold objects, there are the three perfections of equanimity. In this way and so on, the classification of these perfections should be understood.

Ko [V 1.0255] saṅgahoti ettha pana –

Now, as to the question, 'What is the grouping?'—

Yathā vibhāgato tiṃsa-vidhā saṅgahato dasa;

Chappakārāva etāsu, yugaḷādīhi sādhaye.

Just as by classification they are thirtyfold, and by grouping, ten; so too, they are of six kinds. Moreover, among them, they are accomplished by means of pairs and so forth.

Yathā hi esā vibhāgato tiṃsavidhāpi dānapāramiādibhāvato dasavidhā, evaṃ dānasīlakhantivīriyajhānapaññāsabhāvena chabbidhā. Etāsu hi nekkhammapāramī sīlapāramiyā saṅgahitā tassā pabbajjābhāve. Nīvaraṇavivekabhāve pana jhānapāramiyā, kusaladhammabhāve chahipi saṅgahitā, saccapāramī sīlapāramiyā ekadesā eva vacīsaccaviratisaccapakkhe. Ñāṇasaccapakkhe [M 1.0291] pana paññāpāramiyā saṅgahitā, mettāpāramī jhānapāramiyā eva, upekkhāpāramī jhānapaññāpāramīhi, adhiṭṭhānapāramī sabbāhipi saṅgahitāti.

For just as these perfections, though thirtyfold by classification, are tenfold by being the perfection of giving and so on, so too they are sixfold by nature: giving, virtue, patience, energy, absorption, and wisdom. Among these, the perfection of renunciation is included in the perfection of virtue in its aspect of going forth. But in its aspect of seclusion from the hindrances, it is included in the perfection of absorption. In its aspect as a wholesome quality, it is included in all six. The perfection of truth is included only partially in the perfection of virtue, in the aspect of verbal truth and abstinence related to truth. But in the aspect of truth as knowledge, it is included in the perfection of wisdom. The perfection of loving-kindness is included in the perfection of absorption itself. The perfection of equanimity is included in the perfections of absorption and wisdom. The perfection of determination is included in all of them.

Etesañca dānādīnaṃ channaṃ guṇānaṃ aññamaññasambandhānaṃ pañcadasa yugaḷādīni pañcadasa yugaḷādisādhakāni honti. Seyyathidaṃ? Dānasīlayugaḷena parahitāhitānaṃ karaṇākaraṇayugaḷasiddhi, dānakhantiyugaḷena alobhādosayugaḷasiddhi, dānavīriyayugaḷena cāgasutayugaḷasiddhi, dānajhānayugaḷena kāmadosappahānayugaḷasiddhi, dānapaññāyugaḷena ariyayānadhurayugaḷasiddhi, sīlakhantidvayena payogāsayasuddhadvayasiddhi, sīlavīriyadvayena bhāvanādvayasiddhi, sīlajhānadvayena dussīlyapariyuṭṭhānappahānadvayasiddhi, sīlapaññādvayena dānadvayasiddhi, khantivīriyadvayena khamātejadvayasiddhi, khantijhānadukena virodhānurodhappahānadukasiddhi, khantipaññādukena suññatākhantipaṭivedhadukasiddhi, vīriyajhānadukena paggahāvikkhepadukasiddhi, vīriyapaññādukena saraṇadukasiddhi, jhānapaññādukena yānadukasiddhi. Dānasīlakhantitikena lobhadosamohappahānatikasiddhi, dānasīlavīriyatikena bhogajīvitakāyasārādānatikasiddhi, dānasīlajhānatikena puññakiriyavatthutikasiddhi, dānasīlapaññātikena āmisābhayadhammadānatikasiddhīti evaṃ itarehipi tikehi, catukkādīhi ca yathāsambhavaṃ tikāni, catukkādīni ca yojetabbāni.

Of these six qualities beginning with giving, their mutual connections form fifteen pairs and so forth, which accomplish fifteen pairs and so forth. Namely: The pair of giving and virtue accomplishes the pair of doing and not doing what is beneficial and harmful to others. The pair of giving and patience accomplishes the pair of non-greed and non-aversion. The pair of giving and energy accomplishes the pair of relinquishment and learning. The pair of giving and absorption accomplishes the pair of abandoning sensual desire and aversion. The pair of giving and wisdom accomplishes the pair of the noble vehicle and its yoke. The pair of virtue and patience accomplishes the pair of purity in endeavor and disposition. The pair of virtue and energy accomplishes the pair of developments. The pair of virtue and absorption accomplishes the pair of abandoning immorality and obsession. The pair of virtue and wisdom accomplishes the pair of giving. The pair of patience and energy accomplishes the pair of forbearance and power. The pair of patience and absorption accomplishes the pair of abandoning opposition and compliance. The pair of patience and wisdom accomplishes the pair of patience free from aversion and penetration. The pair of energy and absorption accomplishes the pair of exertion and non-distraction. The pair of energy and wisdom accomplishes the pair of refuges. The pair of absorption and wisdom accomplishes the pair of vehicles. The triad of giving, virtue, and patience accomplishes the triad of abandoning greed, aversion, and delusion. The triad of giving, virtue, and energy accomplishes the triad of not taking as essence possessions, life, and body. The triad of giving, virtue, and absorption accomplishes the triad of grounds for meritorious action. The triad of giving, virtue, and wisdom accomplishes the triad of giving material gifts, the gift of fearlessness, and the gift of the Dhamma. In this way, the remaining triads, and tetrads and so on, should be connected as is appropriate.

Evaṃ chabbidhānampi pana imāsaṃ pāramīnaṃ catūhi adhiṭṭhānehi saṅgaho veditabbo. Sabbapāramīnaṃ samūhasaṅgahato hi cattāri adhiṭṭhānāni. Seyyathidaṃ? Saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ, cāgādhiṭṭhānaṃ, upasamādhiṭṭhānaṃ, paññādhiṭṭhānanti. Tattha adhitiṭṭhati etena, ettha vā adhitiṭṭhati, adhiṭṭhānamattameva vā tanti adhiṭṭhānaṃ, saccañca taṃ adhiṭṭhānañca, saccassa vā adhiṭṭhānaṃ, saccaṃ [V 1.0256] vā adhiṭṭhānametassāti saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ. Evaṃ sesesupi. Tattha avisesato tāva katābhinīhārassa anukampitasabbasattassa mahāsattassa paṭiññānurūpaṃ sabbapāramīpariggahato saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ, tesaṃ paṭipakkhapariccāgato cāgādhiṭṭhānaṃ, sabbapāramitāguṇehi upasamanato upasamādhiṭṭhānaṃ. Tehi eva parahitesu upāyakosallato paññādhiṭṭhānaṃ.

Furthermore, the grouping of these perfections, even being sixfold, should be understood by the four determinations. For by way of the collective grouping of all perfections, there are four determinations. Namely: the determination of truth, the determination of relinquishment, the determination of peace, and the determination of wisdom. Therein, 'one determines by means of this,' or 'one determines upon this,' or 'it is merely determination,' thus it is determination. It is both truth and determination; or, it is the determination of truth; or, truth is its determination; thus, it is the determination of truth. The explanation for the remaining terms should be done in the same way. Therein, firstly, in general: for the great being who has made the aspiration and is compassionate to all beings, the determination of truth is the undertaking of all perfections in accordance with his vow. The determination of relinquishment is the abandoning of their opposites. The determination of peace is the calming of defilements through the qualities of all the perfections. The determination of wisdom is the skill in means for the welfare of others by means of those very same qualities.

Visesato pana “yācakānaṃ janānaṃ avisaṃvādetvā dassāmī”ti paṭijānanato, paṭiññaṃ avisaṃvādetvā dānato, dānaṃ avisaṃvādetvā anumodanato[M 1.0292], macchariyādipaṭipakkhapariccāgato, deyyapaṭiggāhakadānadeyyadhammakkhayesu lobhadosamohabhayavūpasamanato, yathārahaṃ yathākālaṃ yathāvidhānañca dānato, paññuttarato ca kusaladhammānaṃ caturadhiṭṭhānapadaṭṭhānaṃ dānaṃ. Tathā saṃvarasamādānassa avītikkamanato, dussīlyapariccāgato, duccaritavūpasamanato, paññuttarato ca caturadhiṭṭhānapadaṭṭhānaṃ sīlaṃ. Yathāpaṭiññaṃ khamanato, katāparādhavikappapariccāgato, kodhapariyuṭṭhānavūpasamanato, paññuttarato ca caturadhiṭṭhānapadaṭṭhānākhanti. Paṭiññānurūpaṃ parahitakaraṇato, visayapariccāgato, akusalavūpasamanato, paññuttarato ca caturadhiṭṭhānapadaṭṭhānaṃ vīriyaṃ. Paṭiññānurūpaṃ lokahitānucintanato, nīvaraṇapariccāgato, cittavūpasamanato, paññuttarato ca caturadhiṭṭhānapadaṭṭhānaṃ jhānaṃ. Yathāpaṭiññaṃ parahitūpāyakosallato, anupāyakiriyapariccāgato, mohajapariḷāhavūpasamanato, sabbaññutāpaṭilābhato ca caturadhiṭṭhānapadaṭṭhānā paññā.

Furthermore, specifically: due to promising, 'I will give to those who ask without deceiving them'; due to giving without failing the promise; due to rejoicing without failing in regard to the gift; due to relinquishing stinginess and other opposing factors; due to the calming of greed, hatred, delusion, and fear in regard to the gift, the recipient, the act of giving, and the exhaustion of the object to be given; due to giving according to what is worthy, according to the time, and according to the arrangement; and due to the pre-eminence of wisdom, giving has the four resolutions as its proximate cause for wholesome states. Likewise, due to not transgressing the undertaking of restraint, due to relinquishing immorality, due to the calming of misconduct, and due to the pre-eminence of wisdom, virtue has the four resolutions as its proximate cause. Due to enduring in accordance with one's promise, due to relinquishing scheming about offenses committed by others, due to the calming of the assault of anger, and due to the pre-eminence of wisdom, patience has the four resolutions as its proximate cause. Due to acting for the welfare of others in accordance with one's promise, due to relinquishing sense-objects, due to calming the unwholesome, and due to the pre-eminence of wisdom, effort has the four resolutions as its proximate cause. Due to repeatedly considering the welfare of the world in accordance with one's promise, due to relinquishing the hindrances, due to the calming of the mind, and due to the pre-eminence of wisdom, absorption has the four resolutions as its proximate cause. Due to skill in the means for the welfare of others in accordance with the promise, due to relinquishing action that is not a means, due to the calming of the torment born of delusion, and due to the attainment of omniscience, wisdom has the four resolutions as its proximate cause.

Tattha ñeyyapaṭiññānuvidhānehi saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ, vatthukāmakilesakāmapariccāgehi cāgādhiṭṭhānaṃ, dosadukkhavūpasamehi upasamādhiṭṭhānaṃ, anubodhapaṭivedhehi paññādhiṭṭhānaṃ. Tividhasaccapariggahitaṃ dosattayavirodhi saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ, tividhacāgapariggahitaṃ dosattayavirodhi cāgādhiṭṭhānaṃ, tividhavūpasamapariggahitaṃ dosattayavirodhi upasamādhiṭṭhānaṃ, tividhañāṇapariggahitaṃ dosattayavirodhi paññādhiṭṭhānaṃ. Saccādhiṭṭhānapariggahitāni cāgūpasamapaññādhiṭṭhānāni avisaṃvādanato, paṭiññānuvidhānato ca. Cāgādhiṭṭhānapariggahitāni saccūpasamapaññādhiṭṭhānāni paṭipakkhapariccāgato, sabbapariccāgaphalattā ca. Upasamādhiṭṭhānapariggahitāni saccacāgapaññādhiṭṭhānāni kilesapariḷāhūpasamanato, kammapariḷāhūpasamanato ca. Paññādhiṭṭhānapariggahitāni saccacāgūpasamādhiṭṭhānāni ñāṇapubbaṅgamato, ñāṇānuparivattanato cāti evaṃ sabbāpi pāramiyo saccappabhāvitā cāgaparibyañjitā upasamopabrūhitā paññāparisuddhā. Saccañhi etāsaṃ janakahetu, cāgo paṭiggāhakahetu, upasamo paribuddhihetu paññā pārisuddhihetu. Tathā ādimhi saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ saccapaṭiññattā, majjhe cāgādhiṭṭhānaṃ katapaṇidhānassa [V 1.0257] parahitāya attapariccāgato, ante upasamādhiṭṭhānaṃ sabbūpasamapariyosānattā. Ādimajjhapariyosānesu paññādhiṭṭhānaṃ tasmiṃ sati sambhavato, asati asambhavato, yathāpaṭiññañca sambhavato.

Among these, the resolution of truth comes to be through acting in accordance with the promise regarding what is to be known. The resolution of relinquishment comes to be through relinquishing sensual objects and sensual defilements. The resolution of peace comes to be through the calming of aversion and suffering. The resolution of wisdom comes to be through understanding accordingly and through penetration. The resolution of truth, comprehended by the threefold truth, is opposed to the triad of faults. The resolution of relinquishment, comprehended by the threefold relinquishment, is opposed to the triad of faults. The resolution of peace, comprehended by the threefold calming, is opposed to the triad of faults. The resolution of wisdom, comprehended by the threefold knowledge, is opposed to the triad of faults. The resolutions of relinquishment, peace, and wisdom are comprehended by the resolution of truth, because of non-deception and acting in accordance with the promise. The resolutions of truth, peace, and wisdom are comprehended by the resolution of relinquishment, due to relinquishing opposing states and because it is the fruit of all relinquishment. The resolutions of truth, relinquishment, and wisdom are comprehended by the resolution of peace, due to the calming of the torment of defilements and the torment of kamma. The resolutions of truth, relinquishment, and peace are comprehended by the resolution of wisdom, because knowledge is the forerunner and because they follow in accordance with knowledge. Thus, all perfections are influenced by truth, made manifest by relinquishment, augmented by peace, and purified by wisdom. Indeed, truth is their generative cause, relinquishment their cause of undertaking, peace their cause of growth, and wisdom their cause of purity. Likewise, in the beginning, there is the resolution of truth, due to the declaration of truth. In the middle, there is the resolution of relinquishment, due to the Bodhisatta who has made an aspiration relinquishing himself for the welfare of others. At the end, there is the resolution of peace, because it is the culmination of the calming of all defilements. In the beginning, middle, and end, there is the resolution of wisdom, because when it is present, they arise, and when it is absent, they do not arise, and because it arises in accordance with the promise.

Tattha [M 1.0293] mahāpurisā satataṃ attahitaparahitakarehi garupiyabhāvakarehi saccacāgādhiṭṭhānehi gihibhūtā āmisadānena pare anuggaṇhanti. Tathā attahitaparahitakarehi, garupiyabhāvakarehi, upasamapaññādhiṭṭhānehi ca pabbajitabhūtā dhammadānena pare anuggaṇhanti.

Therein, great beings, being householders, constantly support others with the gift of material things through the resolutions of truth and relinquishment, which bring about their own welfare and the welfare of others, and which create a state of being respected and loved. Likewise, being renunciants, they support others with the gift of the Dhamma through the resolutions of peace and wisdom, which bring about their own welfare and the welfare of others, and which create a state of being respected and loved.

Tattha antimabhave bodhisattassa caturadhiṭṭhānaparipūraṇaṃ. Paripuṇṇacaturadhiṭṭhānassa hi carimakabhavūpapattīti eke. Tatrāpi hi gabbhāvakkantiabhinikkhamanesu paññādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena sato sampajāno saccādhiṭṭhānapāripūriyā sampatijāto uttarābhimukho sattapadavītihārena gantvā sabbā disā oloketvā saccānuparivattinā vacasā “aggohamasmi lokassa, jeṭṭhohamasmi lokassa, seṭṭhohamasmi lokassā”ti (dī. ni. 2.31; ma. ni. 3.207) tikkhattuṃ sīhanādaṃ nadi, upasamādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena jiṇṇāturamatapabbajitadassāvino catudhammappadesakovidassa yobbanārogyajīvitasampattimadānaṃ upasamo, cāgādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena mahato ñātiparivaṭṭassa, hatthagatassa ca cakkavattirajjassa anapekkhapariccāgoti.

Some say that in the final existence, there is for the Bodhisatta the fulfillment of the four resolutions. Indeed, for one whose four resolutions are fulfilled, there is arising in the final existence. Therein also, at the time of descending into the womb and emerging from it, through the accomplishment of the resolution of wisdom, he is mindful and clearly comprehending. Due to the fulfillment of the resolution of truth, immediately upon being born, facing north, having gone seven steps, and surveying all directions, with words that accord with truth, he uttered the lion's roar three times: 'I am the chief in the world, I am the eldest in the world, I am the best in the world.' Through the accomplishment of the resolution of peace, for the one who has seen the aged, the sick, the dead, and the renunciant, and is skilled in pointing out the four dhammas, there is the calming of the intoxication with the accomplishment of youth, health, and life. Through the accomplishment of the resolution of relinquishment, there is the unconcerned relinquishing of a great circle of relatives and of the sovereignty of a wheel-turning monarch that has come into his hand.

Dutiye ṭhāne abhisambodhiyaṃ caturadhiṭṭhānaparipūraṇanti keci. Tattha hi yathāpaṭiññaṃ saccādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena catunnaṃ ariyasaccānaṃ abhisamayo. Tato hi saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ. Cāgādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena sabbakilesupakkilesapariccāgo. Tato hi cāgādhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ. Upasamādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena paramūpasamasampatti. Tato hi upasamādhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ. Paññādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena anāvaraṇañāṇapaṭilābho. Tato hi paññādhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇanti, taṃ asiddhaṃ abhisambodhiyāpi paramatthabhāvato.

Some say that in the second place, at the time of full awakening, there is the fulfillment of the four resolutions. There, indeed, in accordance with the promise, through the accomplishment of the resolution of truth, there is the direct realization of the four noble truths. Only because of that is the resolution of truth fulfilled. Through the accomplishment of the resolution of relinquishment, there is the relinquishing of all defilements and imperfections. Only because of that is the resolution of relinquishment fulfilled. Through the accomplishment of the resolution of peace, there is the attainment of supreme peace. Only because of that is the resolution of peace fulfilled. Through the accomplishment of the resolution of wisdom, there is the attainment of unobstructed knowledge. Only because of that is the resolution of wisdom fulfilled. But that statement is not established, because full awakening itself is of the nature of ultimate reality.

Tatiye ṭhāne dhammacakkappavattane caturadhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇanti aññe. Tattha hi saccādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa dvādasahi ākārehi ariyasaccadesanāya saccādhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ, cāgādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa saddhammamahāyāgakaraṇena cāgādhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ, upasamādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa sayaṃ upasantassa paresaṃ upasamanena upasamādhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇaṃ, paññādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa [V 1.0258] vineyyānaṃ āsayādiparijānanena paññādhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇanti, tadapi asiddhaṃ apariyositattā buddhakiccassa.

In the third instance, at the setting in motion of the Wheel of Dhamma, others say the four determinations are fulfilled. For, in that case, for one endowed with the determination of truth, the determination of truth is fulfilled by the teaching of the Noble Truths in twelve aspects; for one endowed with the determination of relinquishment, the determination of relinquishment is fulfilled by making the great sacrifice of the good Dhamma; for one endowed with the determination of serenity, the determination of serenity is fulfilled by being oneself pacified and by pacifying others; for one endowed with the determination of wisdom, the determination of wisdom is fulfilled by thoroughly knowing the dispositions, and so forth, of those to be trained. That, too, is not established, because the Buddha's task is not yet finished.

Catutthe [M 1.0294] ṭhāne parinibbāne caturadhiṭṭhānaṃ paripuṇṇanti apare. Tatra hi parinibbutattā paramatthasaccasampattiyā saccādhiṭṭhānaparipūraṇaṃ, sabbūpadhipaṭinissaggena cāgādhiṭṭhānaparipūraṇaṃ, sabbasaṅkhārūpasamena upasamādhiṭṭhānaparipūraṇaṃ, paññāpayojanaparinibbānena paññādhiṭṭhānaparipūraṇanti.

In the fourth instance, at the Parinibbāna, other teachers say the four determinations are fulfilled. For, in that case, because of having attained Parinibbāna, the fulfillment of the determination of truth occurs through the attainment of the ultimate truth; the fulfillment of the determination of relinquishment occurs through the relinquishing of all attachments; the fulfillment of the determination of serenity occurs through the pacification of all formations; and the fulfillment of the determination of wisdom occurs through the complete pacification which is the fruit of wisdom.

Tatra mahāpurisassa visesena mettākhette abhijātiyaṃ saccādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa saccādhiṭṭhānaparipūraṇamabhibyattaṃ, visesena karuṇākhette abhisambodhiyaṃ paññādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa paññādhiṭṭhānaparipūraṇamabhibyattaṃ, visesena muditākhette dhammacakkappavattane cāgādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa cāgādhiṭṭhānaparipūraṇamabhibyattaṃ, visesena upekkhākhette parinibbāne upasamādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa upasamādhiṭṭhānaparipūraṇamabhibyattanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Therein, it should be understood thus: for the Great Being, especially in the sphere of loving-kindness, at his noble birth, the fulfillment of the determination of truth is exceedingly manifest for one endowed with the determination of truth; especially in the sphere of compassion, at the supreme enlightenment, the fulfillment of the determination of wisdom is exceedingly manifest for one endowed with the determination of wisdom; especially in the sphere of sympathetic joy, at the setting in motion of the Wheel of Dhamma, the fulfillment of the determination of relinquishment is exceedingly manifest for one endowed with the determination of relinquishment; and especially in the sphere of equanimity, at the Parinibbāna, the fulfillment of the determination of serenity is exceedingly manifest for one endowed with the determination of serenity.

Tatrāpi saccādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa saṃvāsena sīlaṃ veditabbaṃ, cāgādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa saṃvohārena soceyyaṃ veditabbaṃ, upasamādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa āpadāsu thāmo veditabbo, paññādhiṭṭhānasamudāgatassa sākacchāya paññā veditabbā. Evaṃ sīlājīvacittadiṭṭhivisuddhiyo veditabbā. Tathā saccādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena dosāgatiṃ na gacchati avisaṃvādanato, cāgādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena chandāgatiṃ na gacchati anabhisaṅgato, upasamādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena bhayāgatiṃ na gacchati anuparodhato, paññādhiṭṭhānasamudāgamena mohāgatiṃ na gacchati yathābhūtāvabodhato.

Therein also, for one endowed with the determination of truth, virtue should be known through living together; for one endowed with the determination of relinquishment, purity of livelihood should be known through dealings; for one endowed with the determination of serenity, strength should be known in calamities; for one endowed with the determination of wisdom, wisdom should be known through discussion. Thus, the purifications of virtue, livelihood, mind, and view should be known. Furthermore, through the endowment of the determination of truth, one does not go to a wrong course through hatred, because of not deviating from the truth; through the endowment of the determination of relinquishment, one does not go to a wrong course through desire, because of non-attachment; through the endowment of the determination of serenity, one does not go to a wrong course through fear, because of non-opposition; through the endowment of the determination of wisdom, one does not go to a wrong course through delusion, because of understanding things as they truly are.

Tathā paṭhamena aduṭṭho adhivāseti, dutiyena aluddho paṭisevati, tatiyena abhīto parivajjeti, catutthena asaṃmūḷho vinodeti. Paṭhamena nekkhammasukhuppatti, itarehi pavivekaupasamasambodhisukhuppattiyo honti. Tathā vivekajapītisukhasamādhijapītisukhaapītijakāyasukha satipārisuddhijaupekkhāsukhuppattiyo etehi catūhi yathākkamaṃ hontīti. Evamanekaguṇānubandhehi catūhi adhiṭṭhānehi sabbapāramisamūhasaṅgaho veditabbo. Yathā ca catūhi adhiṭṭhānehi sabbapāramisaṅgaho, evaṃ karuṇāpaññāhipīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Sabbopi hi bodhisambhāro karuṇāpaññāhi saṅgahito. Karuṇāpaññāpariggahitā hi dānādiguṇā mahābodhisambhārā bhavanti buddhattasiddhipariyosānāti. Evametāsaṃ saṅgaho veditabbo.

Furthermore, by the first, being without malice, one endures; by the second, being without greed, one makes use of requisites; by the third, being fearless, one avoids evil; by the fourth, being undeluded, one dispels delusion. By the first, there is the arising of the happiness of renunciation; by the others, there are the arisings of the happiness of seclusion, serenity, and enlightenment. Furthermore, the arisings of joy and happiness born of seclusion, joy and happiness born of concentration, bodily happiness without joy, and the happiness of equanimity born of the purity of mindfulness occur respectively through these four. Thus, the inclusion of the entire group of perfections should be understood through these four determinations, which are connected with many qualities. And just as the inclusion of all perfections is to be understood through the four determinations, so too should it be seen that they are included by compassion and wisdom. For all the requisites of enlightenment are included by compassion and wisdom. Indeed, qualities such as giving, when embraced by compassion and wisdom, become the great requisites for enlightenment, culminating in the attainment of Buddhood. Thus, their inclusion should be understood.

Ko [V 1.0259][M 1.0295] sampādanūpāyoti –

What is the means of accomplishment?

Sabbāsaṃ pana tāsampi, upāyoti sampādane;

Avekallādayo atta-niyyātanādayo matā.

Furthermore, for the accomplishment of all these, non-deficiency and so forth, and self-dedication and so forth, are considered the means.

Sakalassāpi hi puññādisambhārassa sammāsambodhiṃ uddissa anavasesasambharaṇaṃ avekallakāritāyogena, tattha ca sakkaccakāritā ādarabahumānayogena, sātaccakāritā nirantarapayogena, cirakālādiyogo ca antarā avosānāpajjanenāti. Taṃ panassa kālaparimāṇaṃ parato āvi bhavissati. Iti caturaṅgayogo etāsaṃ pāramīnaṃ sampādanūpāyo.

For, with regard to all the requisites of merit and so forth, aiming at perfect self-enlightenment, there is the gathering without remainder through the practice of acting without deficiency; and therein, the practice of acting respectfully through the application of reverence and great esteem; the practice of acting persistently through uninterrupted application; and the application over a long period of time by not coming to a stop in the middle. Furthermore, its measure of time will become manifest later. Thus, this four-factored application is the means for accomplishing these perfections.

Tathā mahāsattena bodhāya paṭipajjantena sammāsambodhāya buddhānaṃ puretarameva attā niyyātetabbo “imāhaṃ attabhāvaṃ buddhānaṃ niyyātemī”ti. Taṃ taṃ pariggahavatthuñca paṭilābhato puretarameva dānamukhe nissajjitabbaṃ “yaṃ kiñci mayhaṃ uppajjanakaṃ jīvitaparikkhārajātaṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ sati yācake dassāmi, tesaṃ pana dinnāvasesaṃ eva mayā paribhuñjitabba”nti.

Furthermore, a Great Being practicing for enlightenment should dedicate himself to the Buddhas for the sake of perfect self-enlightenment even beforehand, thus: 'I dedicate this personality to the Buddhas.' And whatever possession is acquired, it should be relinquished beforehand at the entrance of giving, thinking: 'Whatever kind of life-requisite arises for me, I will give it all if there is a petitioner. Only what remains after having given to them should be used by me.'

Evañhissa sammadeva pariccāgāya kate cittābhisaṅkhāre yaṃ uppajjati pariggahavatthu aviññāṇakaṃ, saviññāṇakaṃ vā, tattha ye ime pubbe dāne akataparicayo, pariggahavatthussa parittabhāvo, uḷāramanuññatā, parikkhayacintāti cattāro dānavinibandhā. Tesu yadā mahābodhisattassa saṃvijjamānesu deyyadhammesu, paccupaṭṭhite ca yācakajane dāne cittaṃ na pakkhandati na kamati, tena niṭṭhamettha gantabbaṃ “addhāhaṃ dāne pubbe akataparicayo, tena me etarahi dātukamyatā citte na saṇṭhātī”ti. So “evaṃ me ito paraṃ dānābhirataṃ cittaṃ bhavissati, handāhaṃ ito paṭṭhāya dānaṃ dassāmi, nanu mayā paṭikacceva pariggahavatthuṃ yācakānaṃ pariccatta”nti dānaṃ deti muttacāgo payatapāṇi vossaggarato yācayogo dānasaṃvibhāgarato. Evaṃ mahāsattassa paṭhamo dānavinibandho hato hoti vihato samucchinno.

Thus, for this Bodhisatta, when the mental volition for relinquishment has been rightly made, whatever object of possession arises—whether inanimate or animate—therein are these four impediments to giving: lack of prior practice in giving, the scarcity of the object of possession, its great agreeableness, and thoughts of its exhaustion. Among these, when there are gift-objects available and a petitioner is present, if the Great Bodhisatta's mind does not leap forward or proceed to giving, this conclusion should be reached by him: 'Surely, I have not previously practiced giving; therefore, the desire to give does not settle in my mind now.' He then thinks, 'Thus, from now on, my mind will delight in giving. Come, from this time on, I shall give a gift. Have I not already relinquished the object of possession to petitioners beforehand?' and gives the gift, being one of open-handed generosity, with a ready hand, delighting in relinquishment, fit to be asked from, and delighting in the proper sharing of gifts. In this way, the Great Being's first impediment to giving is struck down, destroyed, and utterly cut off.

Tathā mahāsatto deyyadhammassa parittabhāve sati paccayavekalle iti paṭisañcikkhati “ahaṃ kho pubbe adānasīlatāya etarahi evaṃ paccayavekallo jāto, tasmā idāni mayā parittena vā hīnena vā yathāladdhena [M 1.0296] deyyadhammena attānaṃ pīḷetvāpi dānameva dātabbaṃ, yenāhaṃ āyatimpi dānapāramiṃ matthakaṃ pāpessāmī”ti so itarītarena dānaṃ deti muttacāgo payatapāṇi [V 1.0260] vossaggarato yācayogo dānasaṃvibhāgarato. Evaṃ mahāsattassa dutiyo dānavinibandho hato hoti vihato samucchinno.

Furthermore, when there is a scarcity of the gift-object and a deficiency of requisites, the Great Being reflects thus: 'Indeed, because of my previous habit of not giving, I have now become thus deficient in requisites. Therefore, now, even by afflicting myself, a gift must be given with whatever small or inferior gift-object has been obtained, by which I shall, in the future, bring the perfection of giving to its peak.' Thus, he gives a gift with one thing or another, being one of open-handed generosity, with a ready hand, delighting in relinquishment, fit to be asked from, and delighting in the proper sharing of gifts. In this way, the Great Being's second impediment to giving is struck down, destroyed, and utterly cut off.

Tathā mahāsatto deyyadhammassa uḷāramanuññatāya adātukamyatācitte uppajjamāne iti paṭisañcikkhati “nanu tayā sappurisa uḷāratamā sabbaseṭṭhā sammāsambodhi abhipatthitā, tasmā tadatthaṃ tayā uḷāramanuññe eva deyyadhamme dātuṃ yuttarūpa”nti. So uḷāraṃ, manuññañca dānaṃ deti muttacāgo payatapāṇi vossaggarato yācayogo dānasaṃvibhāgarato. Evaṃ mahāpurisassa tatiyo dānavinibandho hato hoti vihato samucchinno.

Furthermore, when a mind of unwillingness to give arises in the Great Being due to the magnificence and agreeableness of the gift-object, he reflects thus: 'Have you not, O good man, aspired to the most magnificent, the supreme of all, perfect enlightenment? Therefore, for that purpose, it is proper for you to give gift-objects that are indeed magnificent and agreeable.' He gives a magnificent and agreeable gift, being one of open-handed generosity, with a ready hand, delighting in relinquishment, fit to be asked from, and delighting in the proper sharing of gifts. In this way, the great man's third impediment to giving is struck down, destroyed, and utterly cut off.

Tathā mahāsatto dānaṃ dento yadā deyyadhammassa parikkhayaṃ passati, so iti paṭisañcikkhati “ayaṃ kho bhogānaṃ sabhāvo, yadidaṃ khayadhammatā vayadhammatā, apica me pubbe tādisassa dānassa akatattā evaṃ bhogānaṃ parikkhayo dissati, handāhaṃ yathāladdhena deyyadhammena parittena vā, vipulena vā dānameva dadeyyaṃ, yenāhaṃ āyatiṃ dānapāramiyā matthakaṃ pāpuṇissāmī’ti. So yathāladdhena dānaṃ deti muttacāgo payatapāṇi vossaggarato yācayogo dānasaṃvibhāgarato. Evaṃ mahāsattassa catuttho dānavinibandho hato hoti vihato samucchinno. Evaṃ ye ye dānapāramiyā vinibandhabhūtā anatthā, tesaṃ tesaṃ yathārahaṃ paccavekkhitvā paṭivinodanaṃ upāyo. Yathā ca dānapāramiyā, evaṃ sīlapāramiādīsupi daṭṭhabbaṃ.

Furthermore, the Great Being, while giving a gift, sees the exhaustion of the gift-object and reflects thus: 'This indeed is the nature of possessions—that is, being subject to destruction and decay. Moreover, because such a gift was not made by me previously, this exhaustion of possessions is seen. Come now, I should give a gift with whatever gift-object I have obtained, whether little or abundant, by which I shall, in the future, reach the peak of the perfection of giving.' He gives a gift with what has been obtained, being one of open-handed generosity, with a ready hand, delighting in relinquishment, fit to be asked from, and delighting in the proper sharing of gifts. In this way, the Great Being's fourth impediment to giving is struck down, destroyed, and utterly cut off. Thus, for whatever disadvantages have become impediments to the perfection of giving, having reviewed them appropriately, their dispelling is the means. And as with the perfection of giving, so too should it be understood with the perfections of virtue and the others.

Apica yaṃ mahāsattassa buddhānaṃ attasanniyyātanaṃ, taṃ sammadeva sabbapāramīnaṃ sampādanūpāyo, buddhānañca attānaṃ niyyātetvā ṭhito mahāpuriso tattha tattha bodhisambhārapāripūriyā ghaṭento vāyamanto sarīrassa, sukhūpakaraṇānañca upacchedakesu dussahesupi kiccesu (kicchesu cariyā. aṭṭha. pakiṇṇakakathā) durabhisambhavesupi sattasaṅkhārasamupanītesu anatthesu tibbesu pāṇaharesu “ayaṃ mayā attabhāvo buddhānaṃ pariccatto, yaṃ vā taṃ vā ettha hotū”ti [M 1.0297] tannimittaṃ na kampati na vedhati īsakampi aññathattaṃ na gacchati, kusalārambhe aññadatthu acalādhiṭṭhāno ca hoti, evaṃ attasanniyyātanampi etāsaṃ sampādanūpāyo.

Furthermore, the Great Being's dedication of himself to the Buddhas is indeed the means for the fulfillment of all the perfections. And the great man, who stands having dedicated himself to the Buddhas, while striving and exerting himself here and there for the fulfillment of the requisites of enlightenment—even in the face of unbearable tasks that bring deprivation to his body and means of comfort, in tasks difficult to accomplish, and in severe, life-taking misfortunes brought about by the formations of beings—thinking, 'This personality of mine has been relinquished to the Buddhas—let whatever may be, happen to it,' on account of that, does not tremble, does not waver, and does not go to another state even slightly. On the contrary, in undertaking what is skillful, he is of unshakable resolution. Thus, the dedication of oneself is also a means for the fulfillment of these perfections.

Apica samāsato katābhinīhārassa attani sinehassa pariyādānaṃ, (parisosanaṃ cariyā. aṭṭha. pakiṇṇakakathā) paresu ca sinehassa parivaḍḍhanaṃ etāsaṃ sampādanūpāyo. Sammāsambodhisamadhigamāya hi katamahāpaṇidhānassa mahāsattassa yāthāvato parijānanena sabbesu dhammesu [V 1.0261] anupalittassa attani sineho parikkhayaṃ pariyādānaṃ gacchati, mahākaruṇāsamāyogavasena (samāsevanena cariyā. aṭṭha. pakiṇṇakakathā) pana piyaputte viya sabbasatte sampassamānassa tesu mettākaruṇāsineho parivaḍḍhati, tato ca taṃ tadāvatthānurūpaṃ attaparasantānesu lobhadosamohavigamena vidūrīkatamacchariyādibodhisambhārapaṭipakkho mahāpuriso dānapiyavacanaatthacariyā samānattatāsaṅkhātehi catūhi saṅgahavatthūhi (dī. ni. 3.313; a. ni. 4.32) caturadhiṭṭhānānugatehi accantaṃ janassa saṅgahakaraṇena upari yānattaye avatāraṇaṃ, paripācanañca karoti.

Furthermore, in brief, for one who has made the aspiration, the exhaustion of affection for oneself and the increase of affection for others is the means for the fulfillment of these perfections. Indeed, for the Great Being who has made the great aspiration for the attainment of perfect enlightenment, through true and thorough understanding, being untainted by all things, affection for oneself goes to utter destruction and exhaustion. But, through the power of being endowed with great compassion, while regarding all beings like a dear son, his affection for them through loving-kindness and compassion increases. And from that, according to that particular state, the great man—having, through the removal of greed, hatred, and delusion in his own and others' mental continuities, distanced the opponents of the requisites of enlightenment such as stinginess—with the four bases of sympathy known as giving, endearing speech, beneficial conduct, and impartiality, accompanied by the four determinations, by thoroughly supporting the populace, brings about their entry into and maturation in the three vehicles above.

Mahāsattānañhi mahākaruṇā, mahāpaññā ca dānena alaṅkatā, dānaṃ piyavacanena, piyavacanaṃ atthacariyāya, atthacariyā samānattatāya alaṅkatā, saṅgahitā ca. Tesañhi sabbepi satte attanā nibbisese katvā bodhisambhāresu paṭipajjantānaṃ sabbattha samānasukhadukkhatāya samānattatāsiddhi. Buddhabhūtānampi ca teheva catūhi saṅgahavatthūhi caturadhiṭṭhānena paripūritābhibuddhehi janassa accantikasaṅgahakaraṇena abhivinayanaṃ sijjhati. Dānañhi sammāsambuddhānaṃ cāgādhiṭṭhānena paripūritābhibuddhaṃ. Piyavacanaṃ saccādhiṭṭhānena, atthacariyā paññādhiṭṭhānena, samānattatā upasamādhiṭṭhānena paripūritābhibuddhā. Tathāgatānañhi sabbasāvakapaccekabuddhehi samānattatā parinibbāne. Tatra hi nesaṃ avisesato ekībhāvo. Tenevāha “natthi vimuttiyā nānatta”ti. Honti cettha –

Indeed, for great beings, great compassion and great wisdom are adorned by giving; giving is adorned by pleasant speech, pleasant speech by beneficial conduct, and beneficial conduct by impartiality; and it is also included. For those Bodhisattvas who practice for the requisites of enlightenment, having made all beings without distinction from oneself, the accomplishment of impartiality occurs everywhere due to having equal happiness and suffering. Even for those who have become Buddhas, through those same four bases of sympathy and the four resolutions, which are fulfilled and augmented, the training of beings is accomplished by means of complete cherishing. Indeed, for the Perfectly Enlightened Ones, giving is fulfilled and augmented by the resolution of relinquishment. Pleasant speech is fulfilled and augmented by the resolution of truth, beneficial conduct by the resolution of wisdom, and impartiality is fulfilled and augmented by the resolution of calm. Indeed, for the Tathāgatas, there is impartiality in Parinibbāna together with all disciples and Paccekabuddhas. For there, for them, there is a state of oneness without distinction. Therefore, it was said, 'There is no diversity in liberation.' And here there are these summary verses:

“Sacco cāgī upasanto, paññavā anukampako;

Sambhatasabbasambhāro, kaṃ nāmatthaṃ na sādhaye.

Truthful, generous, peaceful, wise, compassionate, having accumulated all requisites—what purpose indeed could such a great man not accomplish?

Mahākāruṇiko [M 1.0298] satthā, hitesī ca upekkhako;

Nirapekkho ca sabbattha, aho acchariyo jino.

The Teacher is greatly compassionate, a seeker of welfare, and equanimous; and free from attachment in all things. Oh, how wonderful is the Conqueror!

Viratto sabbadhammesu, sattesu ca upekkhako;

Sadā sattahite yutto, aho acchariyo jino.

Dispassionate towards all worldly phenomena, and equanimous towards beings; always engaged in the welfare of beings. Oh, how wonderful is the Conqueror!

Sabbadā sabbasattānaṃ, hitāya ca sukhāya ca;

Uyyutto akilāsū ca, aho acchariyo jino”ti. (cariyā. aṭṭha. pakiṇṇakakathā);

Always for the welfare and for the happiness of all beings, striving and untiring. Oh, how wonderful is the Conqueror!

Kittakena [V 1.0262] kālena sampādananti –

In how much time is the accomplishment?

Paññādhikādibhedena, ugghāṭitaññuādinā;

Tiṇṇampi bodhisattānaṃ, vasā kālo tidhā mato.

By the distinction of one with superior wisdom and so on, and by one of quick understanding and so on; by the power of the three Bodhisattvas, the time is considered threefold.

Heṭṭhimena hi tāva paricchedena cattāri asaṅkhyeyyāni, mahākappānaṃ satasahassañca, majjhimena aṭṭha asaṅkhyeyyāni, mahākappānaṃ satasahassañca, uparimena pana soḷasa asaṅkhyeyyāni, mahākappānaṃ satasahassañca. Ete ca bhedā yathākkamaṃ paññādhikasaddhādhikavīriyādhikavasena veditabbā. Paññādhikānañhi saddhā mandā hoti, paññā tikkhā. Saddhādhikānaṃ paññā majjhimā hoti. Vīriyādhikānaṃ paññā mandā. Paññānubhāvena ca sammāsambodhi abhigantabbāti (su. ni. aṭṭha. 1.34 atthato samānaṃ) aṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttaṃ.

Indeed, first, by the lowest reckoning, there are four incalculables and one hundred thousand great aeons. By the middle reckoning, there are eight incalculables and one hundred thousand great aeons. And by the highest reckoning, there are sixteen incalculables and one hundred thousand great aeons. And these distinctions should be known, in sequence, by the power of the Bodhisattva with superior wisdom, the Bodhisattva with superior faith, and the Bodhisattva with superior energy. For those with superior wisdom, faith is weak and wisdom is sharp. For those with superior faith, wisdom is medium. For those with superior energy, wisdom is weak. And it is stated in the commentary that perfect enlightenment is to be attained by the power of wisdom.

Apare pana “vīriyassa tikkhamajjhimamudubhāvena bodhisattānaṃ ayaṃ kālavibhāgo”ti vadanti, avisesena pana vimuttiparipācanīyānaṃ dhammānaṃ tikkhamajjhimamudubhāvena yathāvuttakālabhedena bodhisambhārā tesaṃ pāripūriṃ gacchantīti tayopete kālabhedā yuttātipi vadanti. Evaṃ tividhā hi bodhisattā abhinīhārakkhaṇe bhavanti eko ugghaṭitaññū, eko vipañcitaññū, eko neyyoti. Tesu yo ugghaṭitaññū, so sammāsambuddhassa sammukhā catuppadagāthaṃ suṇanto gāthāya tatiyapade apariyosite eva chahi abhiññāhi saha paṭisambhidāhi arahattaṃ adhigantuṃ samatthupanissayo hoti, sace sāvakabodhiyaṃ adhimutto siyā.

Others, however, say, 'This division of time for Bodhisattvas is based on the sharpness, moderation, or dullness of their energy.' But in general, they also say that because the requisites for enlightenment of those Bodhisattvas reach fulfillment by the aforesaid distinctions of time due to the sharpness, moderation, or dullness of the qualities that ripen for liberation, these three distinctions of time are suitable. For at the moment of aspiration, Bodhisattvas are of three kinds: one of quick understanding, one of expanded understanding, and one who is to be led. Among them, the Bodhisattva who is of quick understanding, while hearing a four-line stanza in the presence of a Perfectly Enlightened Buddha, has the supporting condition to attain Arahantship together with the six supernormal knowledges and the analytical knowledges even before the third line of the stanza is finished, if he were inclined towards the enlightenment of a disciple.

Dutiyo bhagavato sammukhā catuppadagāthaṃ suṇanto apariyosite eva gāthāya catutthapade chahi abhiññāhi arahattaṃ adhigantuṃ samatthupanissayo hoti, yadi sāvakabodhiyaṃ adhimutto siyā.

The second, while hearing a four-line stanza in the presence of the Blessed One, has the supporting condition to attain Arahantship with the six supernormal knowledges even before the fourth line of the stanza is finished, if he were inclined towards the enlightenment of a disciple.

Itaro [M 1.0299] pana bhagavato sammukhā catuppadagāthaṃ sutvā pariyositāya gāthāya chahi abhiññāhi arahattaṃ adhigantuṃ samatthupanissayo hoti.

The other, however, having heard a four-line stanza in the presence of the Blessed One, has the supporting condition to attain Arahantship with the six supernormal knowledges when the stanza is finished, if he were so inclined.

Tayopete vinā kālabhedena katābhinīhārā, buddhānaṃ santike laddhabyākaraṇā ca anukkamena [V 1.0263] pāramiyo pūrentā yathākkamaṃ yathāvuttabhedena kālena sammāsambodhiṃ pāpuṇanti. Tesu tesu pana kālabhedesu aparipuṇṇesu te te mahāsattā divase divase vessantaradānasadisaṃ mahādānaṃ dentāpi tadanurūpe sīlādisabbapāramidhamme ācinantāpi pañca mahāpariccāge pariccajantāpi ñātatthacariyaṃ lokatthacariyaṃ buddhatthacariyaṃ paramakoṭiṃ pāpentāpi antarāva sammāsambuddhā bhavissantīti netaṃ ṭhānaṃ vijjati. Kasmā? Ñāṇassa aparipaccanato, buddhakārakadhammānañca apariniṭṭhānato. Paricchinnakālanipphāditaṃ viya hi sassaṃ yathāvuttakālaparicchedena parinipphāditā sammāsambodhi tadantarā pana sabbussāhena vāyamantenāpi na sakkā adhigantunti pāramipāripūri yathāvuttakālavisesena sampajjatīti veditabbaṃ.

These three types of Bodhisattvas, having made their aspiration and having received a prediction in the presence of Buddhas, fulfilling the perfections in sequence, attain Perfect Enlightenment in due course by the time with the aforesaid distinctions. However, when those various time-distinctions are unfulfilled, even if those great beings give great gifts daily like the gift of Vessantara, and accumulate all the perfection-qualities such as virtue appropriate to that, and make the five great relinquishments, and bring the conduct for the welfare of relatives, the welfare of the world, and for Buddhahood to the highest peak, it is not a possible case that they will become Perfectly Enlightened Buddhas in the interim. Why? Because of the non-maturation of knowledge and because of the non-completion of the Buddha-making qualities. For just as a crop is produced in a delimited time, so too is Perfect Enlightenment accomplished by the aforesaid delimitation of time; but in the interim, it is not possible to attain it even by striving with all effort. Therefore, it should be known that the fulfillment of the perfections is accomplished by the aforesaid distinction of time.

Ko ānisaṃsoti –

What is the benefit?

Ye te katābhinīhārānaṃ bodhisattānaṃ –

For those Bodhisattvas who have made the aspiration:

“Evaṃ sabbaṅgasampannā, bodhiyā niyatā narā;

Saṃsaraṃ dīghamaddhānaṃ, kappakoṭisatehipi.

Thus endowed with all factors, those beings fixed for enlightenment, wandering for a long period of time, even for hundreds of crores of aeons,

Avīcimhi nuppajjanti, tathā lokantaresu ca;

Nijjhāmataṇhā khuppipāsā, na honti kālakañcikā. (kālakañcikā cariyā. aṭṭha. pakiṇṇakakathā);

They are not born in Avīci, and likewise not in the Lokantarika hells. They do not become Nijjhāmataṇhika petas, Khuppipāsika petas, or Kālakañjika petas.

Na honti khuddakā pāṇā, upapajjantāpi duggatiṃ;

Jāyamānā manussesu, jaccandhā na bhavanti te.

Even if born in a woeful state, they do not become small creatures. When born among humans, they are not blind from birth.

Sotavekallatā natthi, na bhavanti mūgapakkhikā;

Itthibhāvaṃ na gacchanti, ubhatobyañjanapaṇḍakā.

There is no deficiency of the ear faculty, nor do they become mute or paralyzed. They do not attain the state of a female, nor do they become hermaphrodites or sexually indeterminate persons.

Na bhavanti pariyāpannā, bodhiyā niyatā narā;

Muttā ānantarikehi, sabbattha suddhagocarā.

Those beings who are certain of enlightenment are not included [among those with such faults]; they are freed from the heinous crimes and have a pure range in all existences.

Micchādiṭṭhiṃ [V 1.0264][M 1.0300] na sevanti, kammakiriyadassanā;

Vasamānāpi saggesu, asaññaṃ nupapajjare.

They do not associate with wrong views, as they see the reality of kamma and its result; even while living in the heavens, they are not reborn in the realm of non-percipient beings.

Suddhāvāsesu devesu, hetu nāma na vijjati;

Nekkhammaninnā sappurisā, visaṃyuttā bhavābhave;

Caranti lokatthacariyāyo, pūrenti sabbapāramī”ti. (aṭṭhasā. nidānakathā; cariyā. pakiṇṇakakathā; apa. aṭṭha. 1.dūrenidānakathā; jā. aṭṭha. 1.dūrenidānakathā; bu. vaṃ. aṭṭha. 27.dūrenidānakathā); –

For them, the cause to be reborn among the gods of the Pure Abodes does not exist; these virtuous ones are inclined to renunciation, detached amidst good and bad existences; they engage in practices for the welfare of the world and fulfill all the perfections.

Evaṃ saṃvaṇṇitā ānisaṃsā, ye ca “sato sampajāno ānanda bodhisatto tusitā kāyā cavitvā mātukucchiṃ okkamatī”tiādinā (ma. ni. 3.204) soḷasa acchariyabbhutadhammappakārā, ye ca “sītaṃ byapagataṃ hoti, uṇhañca vūpasamatī”tiādinā, (khu. ni. 4-313 piṭṭhe) “jāyamāne kho sāriputta, bodhisatte ayaṃ dasasahassilokadhātu saṅkampati sampakampati sampavedhatī”tiādinā ca dvattiṃsa pubbanimittappakārā, ye vā panaññepi bodhisattānaṃ adhippāyasamijjhanaṃ, kammādīsu ca vasibhāvoti evamādayo tattha tattha jātakabuddhavaṃsādīsu dassitappakārā ānisaṃsā, te sabbepi etāsaṃ ānisaṃsā, tathā yathānidassitabhedā alobhādosādiguṇayugaḷādayo cāti veditabbā.

Thus, the benefits that have been expounded; and the sixteen kinds of wonderful and marvelous phenomena beginning with, “Mindful and clearly aware, Ānanda, the Bodhisatta passed away from the Tusita realm and entered his mother’s womb”; and the thirty-two kinds of preliminary signs beginning with, “The cold is dispelled, and the heat is subdued,” and also with, “When the Bodhisatta is born, Sāriputta, this ten-thousandfold world system trembles, shakes, and quakes”; and whatever other kinds of benefits shown in various places such as the Jātakas and the Buddhavamsa—such as the fulfillment of the Bodhisattas' aspirations and their mastery over kamma and so forth—all these are the benefits of these perfections. Likewise, the pairs of qualities such as non-greed and non-hatred, with their distinctions as indicated, should also be understood as benefits.

Apica yasmā bodhisatto abhinīhārato paṭṭhāya sabbasattānaṃ pitusamo hoti hitesitāya, dakkhiṇeyyako garu bhāvanīyo paramañca puññakkhettaṃ hoti guṇavisesayogena, yebhuyyena ca manussānaṃ piyo hoti, amanussānaṃ piyo hoti, devatāhi anupālīyati, mettākaruṇāparibhāvitasantānatāya vāḷamigādīhi ca anabhibhavanīyo hoti, yasmiṃ yasmiñca sattanikāye paccājāyati, tasmiṃ tasmiṃ uḷārena vaṇṇena uḷārena yasena uḷārena sukhena uḷārena balena uḷārena ādhipateyyena aññe satte abhibhavati puññavisesayogato.

Furthermore, because the Bodhisatta, from the time of his aspiration, is like a father to all beings due to his seeking of their welfare, and because of his special qualities, he is worthy of offerings, venerable, worthy of esteem, and a supreme field of merit. For the most part, he is dear to humans and dear to non-humans, and is protected by deities. Because his mental continuum is pervaded by loving-kindness and compassion, he is unconquerable by wild beasts and the like. And in whatever community of beings he is reborn, due to his special merit, he righteously surpasses other beings with his excellent appearance, excellent retinue, excellent happiness, excellent strength, and excellent sovereignty.

Appābādho hoti appātaṅko, suvisuddhā cassa saddhā hoti suvisadā, suvisuddhaṃ vīriyaṃ, sati samādhi paññā suvisadā, mandakileso hoti mandadaratho mandapariḷāho, kilesānaṃ mandabhāveneva subbaco hoti padakkhiṇaggāhī, khamo hoti sorato, sakhilo hoti paṭisandhārakusalo[M 1.0301], akodhano hoti anupanāhī, amakkhī hoti apaḷāsī, anissukī hoti amaccharī, asaṭho hoti amāyāvī, athaddho hoti anatimānī, asāraddho hoti appamatto[V 1.0265], parato upatāpasaho hoti paresaṃ anupatāpī, yasmiñca gāmakhette paṭivasati, tattha sattānaṃ bhayādayo upaddavā yebhuyyena anuppannā nuppajjanti, uppannā ca vūpasamanti, yesu ca apāyesu uppajjati, na tattha pacurajano viya dukkhena adhimattaṃ pīḷīyati, bhiyyoso mattāya saṃvegabhayamāpajjati. Tasmā mahāpurisassa yathārahaṃ tasmiṃ tasmiṃ bhave labbhamānā ete sattānaṃ pitusamatādakkhiṇeyyatādayo guṇavisesā ānisaṃsāti veditabbā.

He has few illnesses and few afflictions. His faith is exceptionally pure and bright; his energy is exceptionally pure; his mindfulness, concentration, and wisdom are exceptionally bright. He has few defilements and little anguish. Because his defilements are few, he is easy to admonish and receptive to what is excellent. He is patient and gentle in conduct. He is affable and skilled in friendly speech. He is not given to anger or resentment. He is not contemptuous or spiteful. He is not envious or selfish. He is not devious or deceitful. He is not harsh or arrogant. He is not aggressive but is heedful. He can endure affliction from others and does not cause affliction to others. In whatever village or region he dwells, for the most part, dangers and calamities that have not yet arisen do not arise for the beings there, and those that have arisen subside. And in whichever woeful states he is reborn, he is not intensely afflicted by suffering like a common worldling; rather, he experiences an even greater degree of spiritual urgency and fear. Therefore, these special qualities—such as being like a father to beings and being worthy of offerings—which are obtained by the great being in each existence as is fitting, should be understood as the benefits of the perfections.

Tathā āyusampadā rūpasampadā kulasampadā issariyasampadā ādeyyavacanatā mahānubhāvatāti etepi mahāpurisassa pāramīnaṃ ānisaṃsāti veditabbā. Tattha āyusampadā nāma tassaṃ tassaṃ upapattiyaṃ dīghāyukatā ciraṭṭhitikatā, tāya yathāraddhāni kusalasamādānāni pariyosāpeti, bahuñca kusalaṃ upacinoti. Rūpasampadā nāma abhirūpatā dassanīyatā pāsādikatā, tāya rūpappamāṇānaṃ sattānaṃ pasādāvaho hoti sambhāvanīyo. Kulasampadā nāma uḷāresu kulesu abhinibbatti, tāya [jātimadādimadasattānampi (madamattānampi cariyā. aṭṭha. pakiṇṇakakathā)] upasaṅkamanīyo hoti payirupāsanīyo, tena te nibbisevane karonti. Issariyasampadā nāma mahāvibhavatā, mahesakkhatā, mahāparivāratā ca, tāhi saṅgahitabbe catūhi saṅgahavatthūhi (dī. ni. 3.313; a. ni. 1.256) saṅgahituṃ, niggahetabbe dhammena niggahetuñca samattho hoti. Ādeyyavacanatā nāma saddheyyatā paccayikatā, tāya sattānaṃ pamāṇabhūto hoti, alaṅghanīyā cassa āṇā hoti. Mahānubhāvatā nāma pabhāvamahantatā, tāya parehi na abhibhuyyati, sayameva pana pare aññadatthu abhibhavati dhammena, samena, yathābhūtaguṇehi ca, evametesaṃ āyusampadādayo mahāpurisassa pāramīnaṃ ānisaṃsā, sayañca aparimāṇassa puññasambhārassa parivuddhihetubhūtā yānattaye sattānaṃ avatāraṇassa paripācanassa kāraṇabhūtāti veditabbā.

Likewise, the perfection of lifespan, the perfection of beauty, the perfection of lineage, the perfection of sovereignty, trustworthiness of speech, and great power should also be understood as benefits of the great being's perfections. Herein, the perfection of lifespan means longevity and long-lasting existence in each rebirth; through this, one brings to completion the wholesome undertakings one has begun and accumulates much merit. The perfection of beauty means being handsome, pleasant to see, and inspiring; through this, one inspires confidence in beings for whom beauty is the measure and becomes worthy of esteem. The perfection of lineage means being born into eminent families; through this, one becomes approachable and worthy of being attended upon, even by beings intoxicated with pride in their birth, and they constantly associate with him. The perfection of sovereignty means having great wealth, high status, and a large retinue; through these, one is able to gather those who should be gathered by means of the four bases of sympathy, and to righteously restrain those who should be restrained. Trustworthiness of speech means being credible and reliable; through this, one becomes a standard for beings, and one's command is unassailable. Great power means greatness of influence; through this, one is not overcome by others, but rather, one righteously, justly, and with one's true qualities, overcomes others. Thus, these perfections of lifespan and so on are the benefits of the great being's perfections. And they themselves are a cause for the growth of an immeasurable accumulation of merit and a reason for the guiding and maturing of beings in the three vehicles. This should be understood.

Kiṃ [M 1.0302] phalanti –

What is their fruit?

Sammāsambuddhatā tāsaṃ, jaññā phalaṃ samāsato;

Vitthārato anantāpa-meyyā guṇagaṇā matā.

In brief, the state of Perfect Self-Enlightenment should be known as their fruit; in detail, the infinite and immeasurable collections of qualities of a Buddha are to be known as their fruit.

Samāsato hi tāva sammāsambuddhabhāvo etāsaṃ phalaṃ. Vitthārato pana bāttiṃsamahāpurisalakkhaṇa (dī. ni. 2.33 ādayo; 3.198; ma. ni. 2.386) asītānubyañjana, byāmappabhādianekaguṇagaṇasamujjalarūpakāyasampattiadhiṭṭhānā dasabala- (ma. ni. 4.8; a. ni. 10.21) catuvesārajja- [V 1.0266] (a. ni. 4.8) chaasādhāraṇañāṇaaṭṭhārasāveṇikabuddhadhamma- (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 3.305;) pabhutianantāparimāṇaguṇasamudayopasobhinī dhammakāyasirī, yāvatā pana buddhaguṇā ye anekehipi kappehi sammāsambuddhenāpi vācāya pariyosāpetuṃ na sakkā, idameva tāsaṃ phalaṃ. Vuttañcetaṃ bhagavatā –

In brief, indeed, the state of a Perfectly Self-Enlightened Buddha is the fruit of these perfections. In detail, however, there is both the perfection of the physical body—resplendent with a collection of many qualities such as the thirty-two marks of a great man, the eighty minor characteristics, and the fathom-wide radiance—and the glory of the Dhamma-body, adorned with a collection of endless and immeasurable qualities, beginning with the four resolutions, the ten powers, the four kinds of fearlessness, the six kinds of knowledge not shared by others, and the eighteen unique Buddha-qualities. Furthermore, whatever qualities of a Buddha exist that cannot be fully described with speech even by a Perfectly Self-Enlightened Buddha over many eons, this itself is the fruit of those perfections. And this was said by the Blessed One:

“Buddhopi buddhassa bhaṇeyya vaṇṇaṃ,

Kappampi ce aññamabhāsamāno;

Khīyetha kappo ciradīghamantare,

Vaṇṇo na khīyetha tathāgatassā”ti. (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 1.304; 3.141; udā. aṭṭha. 53; cariyā. aṭṭha. nidānakathā, pakiṇṇakakathā) –

“Even a Buddha, speaking of nothing else, might declare the praise of a Buddha for an entire eon; in that long interval, the eon would be exhausted, but the praise of the Tathāgata would not be exhausted.”

Evamettha pāramīsu pakiṇṇakakathā veditabbā.

Thus, the miscellaneous discourse regarding these perfections should be understood herein.

Evaṃ yathāvuttāya paṭipadāya yathāvuttavibhāgānaṃ pāramīnaṃ pūritabhāvaṃ sandhāyāha “samatiṃsa pāramiyo pūretvā”ti. Satipi mahāpariccāgānaṃ dānapāramibhāve pariccāgavisesabhāvadassanatthaṃ, visesasambhāratādassanatthaṃ, sudukkarabhāvadassanatthañca tesaṃ visuṃ gahaṇaṃ, tatoyeva ca aṅgapariccāgato nayanapariccāgassa, pariggahapariccāgabhāvasāmaññepi dhanarajjapariccāgato puttadārapariccāgassa visuṃ gahaṇaṃ kataṃ, tathāyeva ācariyadhammapālattherena (dī. ni. ṭī. 1.7) vuttaṃ. Ācariyasāriputtattherenapi aṅguttaraṭīkāyaṃ, (a. ni. ṭī. 1.ekapuggalavaggassa paṭhame) katthaci pana puttadārapariccāge visuṃ katvā nayanapariccāgamaññatra jīvitapariccāgaṃ vā pakkhipitvā rajjapariccāgamaññatra pañca mahāpariccāge vadanti.

Thus, with reference to the state of having fulfilled the perfections with their divisions as described, by means of the practice as described, the teacher said: 'having fulfilled the thirty perfections.' Although the great sacrifices are a state of the perfection of giving, their separate mention is made to show that they are a special kind of sacrifice, to show that they are a special accumulation, and to show that they are extremely difficult to perform. For that very reason, the sacrifice of the eyes is taken separately from the sacrifice of limbs; and although there is the commonality of being the sacrifice of possessions, the sacrifice of children and wife is taken separately from the sacrifice of wealth and kingdom. Just so was it stated by the teacher, the Elder Dhammapāla. It was also stated by the teacher, the Elder Sāriputta, in the Aṅguttara-ṭīkā. In some cases, however, the teachers speak of five great sacrifices by treating the sacrifice of children and wife as separate, and by excluding the sacrifice of the eyes while including the sacrifice of life, or by excluding the sacrifice of the kingdom.

Gatapaccāgatikavattasaṅkhātāya [M 1.0303] (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 1.9; ma. ni. aṭṭha. 1.10.9; saṃ. ni. aṭṭha. 3.5.368; vibha. aṭṭha. 523; su. ni. aṭṭha. 1.1.35) pubbabhāgapaṭipadāya saddhiṃ abhiññāsamāpattinipphādanaṃ pubbayogo. Dānādīsuyeva sātisayapaṭipattinipphādanaṃ pubbacariyā. Yā vā cariyāpiṭakasaṅgahitā, sā pubbacariyā. Keci pana “abhinīhāro pubbayogo. Dānādipaṭipatti vā kāyavivekavasena ekacariyā vā pubbacariyā”ti vadanti. Dānādīnañceva appicchatādīnañca saṃsāranibbānesu ādīnavānisaṃsānañca [V 1.0267] vibhāvanavasena, sattānaṃ bodhittaye patiṭṭhāpanaparipācanavasena ca pavattā kathā dhammakkhānaṃ. Ñātīnamatthassa cariyā ñātatthacariyā, sāpi karuṇāyanavaseneva. Ādi-saddena lokatthacariyādayo saṅgaṇhāti. Kammassakatāñāṇavasena, anavajjakammāyatanasippāyatanavijjāṭṭhānaparicayavasena, khandhāyatanādiparicayavasena, lakkhaṇattayatīraṇavasena ca ñāṇacāro buddhicariyā, sā panatthato paññāpāramīyeva, ñāṇasambhāradassanatthaṃ pana visuṃ gahaṇaṃ. Koṭinti pariyantaṃ ukkaṃsaṃ. Tathā amhākampi bhagavā āgatoti etthāpi “dānapāramiṃ pūretvā”tiādinā sambandho.

The accomplishment of higher knowledges and meditative attainments, together with the preliminary practice known as gatapaccāgatikavatta (the observance of going and returning), is pubbayoga (prior endeavor). The accomplishment of exceptionally excellent practice in giving and so forth is pubbacariyā (prior conduct). Alternatively, that conduct which is included in the Cariyāpiṭaka is also pubbacariyā. Some, however, say: 'Aspiration is pubbayoga. The practice of giving and so forth, or solitary practice through bodily seclusion, is pubbacariyā.' The teaching of the Dhamma (dhammakkhānaṃ) is a discourse that proceeds by way of explaining the dangers and benefits in saṃsāra and nibbāna regarding giving and so forth, and qualities like having few wishes, and by way of establishing and maturing beings in the threefold enlightenment. Conduct for the welfare of relatives is ñātatthacariyā, and that too is by way of compassion. The term 'ādi' (and so forth) includes conduct for the welfare of the world and other such practices. The practice of wisdom (buddhicariyā) is the movement of knowledge by way of understanding the ownership of deeds (kammassakatā), by way of familiarity with blameless bases of action, skills, and fields of knowledge, by way of familiarity with the aggregates, sense bases, and so forth, and by way of contemplating the three characteristics. In essence, this is the perfection of wisdom itself. However, it is separately mentioned to show the accumulation of knowledge. 'Koṭi' means the limit or highest point. Similarly, here too, the statement 'Thus the Blessed One has come to us' is connected with phrases like 'having fulfilled the perfection of giving' and so forth.

Evaṃ pāramipūraṇavasena “tathā āgato”ti padassatthaṃ dassetvā idāni bodhipakkhiyadhammavasenapi dassento “cattāro satipaṭṭhāne”tiādimāha. Tattha satipaṭṭhānādiggahaṇena āgamanapaṭipadaṃ matthakaṃ pāpetvā dasseti maggaphalapakkhikānaññeva gahetabbattā, vipassanāsaṅgahitā eva vā satipaṭṭhānādayo daṭṭhabbā pubbabhāgapaṭipadāya gahaṇato. Bhāvetvāti uppādetvā. Brūhetvāti vaḍḍhetvā. Ettha ca “yena abhinīhārenā”tiādinā āgamanapaṭipadāyaādiṃ dasseti, “dānapāramiṃ pūretvā”tiādinā majjhe, “cattāro satipaṭṭhāne”tiādinā pariyosānaṃ. Tasmā “āgato”ti vuttassa āgamanassa kāraṇabhūtapaṭipadāvisesadassanaṃyeva tiṇṇaṃ nayānaṃ visesoti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Idāni yathāvuttena atthayojanattayena siddhaṃ paṭhamakāraṇameva gāthābandhavasena dassetuṃ “yathevā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Tattha idhalokamhi vipassiādayo munayo sabbaññubhāvaṃ yathāvuttena kāraṇattayena āgatā yatheva, tathā pañcahi cakkhūhi cakkhumā ayaṃ sakyamunipi yena kāraṇena āgato, tenesa tathāgato nāma vuccatīti yojanā.

Having thus shown the meaning of the phrase 'thus come' by way of fulfilling the perfections, he now shows it also by way of the factors of enlightenment, saying 'the four foundations of mindfulness,' etc. Herein, by mentioning the foundations of mindfulness and so forth, he shows the path of arrival brought to its culmination, since only those factors pertaining to the path and fruit should be taken; or, the foundations of mindfulness and so forth should be understood as included in insight, because of their being taken up by the preliminary practice. 'Having developed' means having produced. 'Having cultivated' means having increased. And here, by 'by which aspiration,' etc., he shows the beginning of the path of arrival; by 'having fulfilled the perfection of giving,' etc., the middle; and by 'the four foundations of mindfulness,' etc., the end. Therefore, it should be seen that the distinction between the three methods is precisely the showing of the particular practice that is the cause of the arrival spoken of as 'come.' Now, to show in verse form the first cause, established by the threefold explanation of meaning as stated, it is said 'just as,' etc. Herein, the interpretation is: just as in this world the sages, Vipassī and others, arrived at the state of omniscience by the three causes as stated, so too, by that cause by which this Sakyan sage, the one with the five eyes, arrived, for that reason he is called 'Tathāgata' (Thus Come One).

Sampatijātoti [M 1.0304] manussānaṃ hatthato muccitvā muhuttajāto, na pana mātukucchito nikkhantamatto mātukucchito nikkhantamattañhi mahāsattaṃ paṭhamaṃ brahmāno suvaṇṇajālena paṭiggaṇhiṃsu, tesaṃ hatthato cattāro mahārājāno ajinappaveṇiyā, tesaṃ hatthato manussā dukūlacumbaṭakena paṭiggaṇhiṃsu, “manussānaṃ hatthato muccitvā pathaviyaṃ patiṭṭhito”ti (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 2.31) vakkhati. “Kathañcā”tiādi vitthāradassanaṃ. Yathāha bhagavā mahāpadānadesanāyaṃ. Setamhi chatteti dibbasetacchatte. Anuhīramāneti dhāriyamāne. “Anudhāriyamāne”tipi idāni pāṭho. “Ettha ca chattaggahaṇeneva khaggadīni pañca kakudhabhaṇḍānipi gahitānevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Khaggatālavaṇṭamorahatthakavālabījanīuṇhīsapaṭṭāpi hi chattena saha tadā upaṭṭhitā ahesuṃ. Chattādīniyeva ca tadā paññāyiṃsu, na chattādigāhakā”ti [V 1.0268] (dī. ni. ṭī. 1.7) ācariyadhammapālattherena vuttaṃ, ācariyasāriputtattherenāpi aṅguttaraṭīkāyaṃ (a. ni. ṭī. 1.ekapuggalavaggassa paṭhame) evaṃ sati tālavaṇṭādīnampi kakudhabhaṇḍasamaññā. Apica khaggādīni kakudhabhaṇḍāni, tadaññānipi tālavaṇṭādīni tadā upaṭṭhitānīti adhippāyena tathā vuttaṃ.

'Just born' means being freed from the hands of humans a moment after birth, not merely emerging from the mother's womb. Indeed, when the Great Being had just emerged from his mother's womb, the Brahmās first received him with a golden net. From their hands, the Four Great Kings received him with a spread of black deerskin. From their hands, humans received him with a coil of fine cloth. It will be said: "Freed from the hands of humans, he stood on the earth." The passage beginning "And how?" is for showing the detail, as the Blessed One declared in the Mahāpadāna discourse. 'Under a white parasol' means a divine white parasol. 'Being held over' means being held. There is also now the reading 'being continuously held over'. And here it should be understood that by the mention of the parasol alone, the five royal regalia beginning with the sword are also included. Indeed, the sword, palm-leaf fan, peacock-feather fan, yak-tail whisk, and diadem also appeared at that time together with the parasol. And only the parasol and so on were visible then, not those who held the parasol and so on. This was stated by the teacher, the Elder Dhammapāla. The teacher, the Elder Sāriputta, also stated in the Aṅguttara Subcommentary that in this case, the palm-leaf fan and so on also have the designation of 'royal regalia'. Furthermore, it was stated thus with the intention that the royal regalia beginning with the sword, and others besides them such as the palm-leaf fan, were present at that time.

Sabbā ca disāti dasa disā. Anuviloketīti puññānubhāvena lokavivaraṇapāṭihāriye jāte paññāyamānaṃ dasasahassilokadhātuṃ maṃsacakkhunāva oloketīti attho. Nayidaṃ sabbadisānuvilokanaṃ sattapadavītihāruttarakālaṃ paṭhamamevānuvilokanato. Mahāsatto hi manussānaṃ hatthato muccitvā puratthimaṃ disaṃ olokesi. Tattha devamanussā gandhamālādīhi pūjayamānā “mahāpurisa idha tumhehi sadisopi natthi, kuto tayā uttaritaro”ti āhaṃsu. Evaṃ catasso disā catasso anudisā heṭṭhā uparīti sabbā disāanuviloketvā sabbattha attanā sadisamadisvā “ayaṃ uttarā disā”ti sattapadavītihārena agamāsīti ācariyadhammapālattherena (dī. ni. ṭī. 1.7) ācariyasāriputtattherena (a. ni. ṭī. 1.ekapuggalavaggassa paṭhame) ca vuttaṃ. Mahāpadānasuttaṭṭhakathāyampi (dī. ni. aṭṭha. 2.31) evameva vaṇṇitaṃ. Tasmā sattapadavītihārato paṭhamaṃ sabbadisānuvilokanaṃ katvā sattapadavītihārena gantvā tadupari āsabhiṃ vācaṃ bhāsatīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Idha, pana aññāsu ca aṭṭhakathāsu samehi [M 1.0305] pādehi patiṭṭhahanato paṭṭhāya yāva āsabhīvācābhāsanaṃ tāva yathākkamaṃ eva pubbanimittabhāvaṃ vibhāvento “sattamapadūpari ṭhatvā sabbadisānuvilokanaṃ sabbaññutānāvaraṇañāṇapaṭilābhassā”tiādīni vadati, evampi yathā na virujjhati, tathā eva attho gahetabbo. “Sattamapadūpari ṭhatvā”ti ca pāṭho pacchā pamādalekhavasena edisena vacanakkamena mahāpadānaṭṭhakathāyamadissamānattāti. Āsabhinti uttamaṃ, akampanikaṃ vā, nibbhayanti attho. Usabhassa idanti hi āsabhaṃ, sūrabhāvo, tena yuttattā panāyaṃ vācā “āsabhī”ti vuccati. Aggoti sabbapaṭhamo. Jeṭṭho, seṭṭhoti ca tasseva vevacanaṃ. Saddatthamattato pana aggoti guṇehi sabbapadhāno. Jeṭṭhoti guṇavaseneva sabbesaṃ vuddhatamo, guṇehi mahallakatamoti vuttaṃ hoti. Seṭṭhoti guṇavaseneva sabbesaṃ pasaṭṭhatamo. Lokassāti vibhattāvadhibhūte nissakkatthe sāmivacanaṃ. Ayamantimā jāti, natthi dāni punabbhavoti imasmiṃ attabhāve pattabbaṃ arahattaṃ byākāsi tabbaseneva punabbhavābhāvato.

'And all directions' means the ten directions. 'He surveys' means that through the power of his merit, when the miracle of the world-opening occurred, he looked upon the ten-thousandfold world system with his physical eye alone; this is the meaning. This surveying of all directions does not happen after the seven-step stride, because the surveying was done first. Indeed, the Great Being, freed from the hands of humans, looked toward the eastern direction. There, devas and humans, worshipping with perfumes, garlands, and so on, said: 'Great Being, here there is no one equal to you, whence one superior?' In this way, having surveyed all directions—the four cardinal directions, the four intermediate directions, below, and above—and seeing no one equal to himself anywhere, he went forth with a seven-step stride, thinking, 'This is the northern direction.' This was stated by the teacher, the Elder Dhammapāla, and by the teacher, the Elder Sāriputta. In the commentary to the Mahāpadāna Sutta, it is explained in this very way. Therefore, it should be understood that having first surveyed all directions before the seven-step stride, and having gone forth with the seven-step stride, upon it he utters the bull-like speech. Here, however, and in other commentaries, explaining the state of being a preliminary sign in sequence from the standing on level feet up to the uttering of the bull-like speech, it says such things as: 'having stood upon the seventh step, the surveying of all directions is a preliminary sign for the attainment of the knowledge of omniscience and the unobstructed knowledge.' Even so, the meaning should be understood in such a way that it is not contradictory. The reading 'having stood upon the seventh step' is a later one, arising from a careless scribe, because such a sequence of words is not seen in the Mahāpadāna commentary. 'Bull-like' means supreme, or unshakable, fearless; this is the meaning. Indeed, because it is of a bull, it is 'bull-like'; the state of heroism is obtained. Because this speech is endowed with that, it is called 'bull-like'. 'Foremost' means the first of all. 'Eldest' and 'best' are its synonyms. However, from the mere meaning of the word, 'foremost' means chief of all through virtues. 'Eldest' means, by the power of virtue alone, the most senior of all; it means the most venerable through virtues. 'Best' means, by the power of virtue alone, the most praised of all. The word 'of the world' is a genitive used in the sense of an ablative of separation, marking a boundary. 'This is the final birth, there is now no renewed existence'—with this, he prophesied the Arahantship to be attained in this existence, because by the power of that, there is no renewed existence.

Idāni tathāgamanaṃ sambhāvento “tañcassā”tiādimāha. Pubbanimittabhāvena tathaṃ avitathanti sambandho. Visesādhigamānanti guṇavisesādhigamānaṃ. Tadevatthaṃ vitthārato dasseti “yañhī”tiādinā[V 1.0269]. Tattha yanti kiriyāparāmasanaṃ, tena “patiṭṭhahī”ti ettha pakatiyatthaṃpatiṭṭhānakiriyaṃ parāmasati. Idamassāti idaṃ patiṭṭhahanaṃ assa bhagavato. Paṭilābhasadde sāminiddeso cesa, kattuniddeso vā. Pubbanimittanti tappaṭilābhasaṅkhātassa āyatiṃ uppajjamānakassa hitassa paṭhamaṃ pavattaṃ sañjānanakāraṇaṃ. Bhagavato hi acchariyabbhutaguṇavisesādhigamane pañca mahāsupinādayo viya etāni sañjānananimittāni pātubhavanti, yathā taṃ loke puññavantānaṃ puññaphalavisesādhigamaneti.

Now, extolling that going forth, he said the passage beginning 'And that of his'. The connection is: 'As a preliminary sign, it was true and not otherwise.' 'Of the attainments of distinction' means of the attainments of special qualities. He shows that very meaning in detail with the passage beginning 'For which'. Therein, 'which' is a reference to an action; by it, in the word 'he stood', it refers to the action of standing, which is its natural meaning. 'This of his' means this standing was of that Blessed One. And this 'of his' is an indication of the possessive in the word 'attainment', or it is an indication of the agent. 'A preliminary sign' is the cause for knowing, which occurs first, of a future benefit designated as that attainment. Indeed, for the Blessed One, at the time of attaining marvelous and wonderful special qualities, these signs for knowing appear, like the five great dreams and so on; just as in the world, for meritorious people, signs for knowing appear at the time of attaining the special fruit of their merit.

Sabbalokuttarabhāvassāti sabbalokānamuttamabhāvassa, sabbalokātikkamanabhāvassa vā. Satta padāni sattapadaṃ, tassa vītihāro visesena atiharaṇaṃ sattapadavītihāro, sattapadanikkhepoti attho. So pana samagamane dvinnaṃ padānamantare muṭṭhiratanamattanti vuttaṃ.

'Of the state of being superior to all worlds' means of the state of being supreme over all worlds, or of the state of transcending all worlds. Seven steps are a 'seven-step'. The 'stride' of that is a special carrying forward. The meaning of 'seven-step stride' is 'the placing of seven steps'. But it is said that for that Bodhisatta, in his even gait, the space between his two feet was the measure of a fist-gem.

“Anekasākhañca [M 1.0306] sahassamaṇḍalaṃ,

Chattaṃ marū dhārayumantalikkhe;

Suvaṇṇadaṇḍā vītipatanti cāmarā,

Na dissare cāmarachattagāhakā”ti. (su. ni. 693); –

“Having innumerable branches and a thousand circles, the devas held the parasol in the sky; chowries with golden staffs were waved, yet the holders of the chowries and the parasol were not seen.”

Suttanipāte nāḷakasutte āyasmatā ānandattherena vuttaṃ nidānagāthāpadaṃ sandhāya “suvaṇṇadaṇḍā vītipatanti cāmarāti etthā”ti vuttaṃ. Etthāti hi etasmiṃ gāthāpadeti attho. Mahāpadānasutte anāgatattā pana cāmarukkhepassa tathā vacanaṃ daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tattha āgatānusārena hi idha pubbanimittabhāvaṃ vadati, camaro nāma migaviseso. Yassa vālena rājakakudhabhūtaṃ vālabījaniṃ karonti, tassa ayanti cāmarī. Tassā ukkhepo tathā, vutto soti vuttacāmarukkhepo. Arahattavimuttivaravimalasetacchattapaṭilābhassāti arahattaphalasamāpattisaṅkhātavaravimalasetacchattapaṭilābhassa. Sattamapadūparīti ettha pada-saddo padavaḷañjanavācako, tasmā sattamassa padavaḷañjanassa uparīti attho. Sabbaññutaññāṇameva sabbattha appaṭihatacāratāya anāvaraṇanti āha “sabbaññutānāvaraṇañāṇapaṭilābhassā”ti. Tathā ayaṃ bhagavā…pe… pubbanimittabhāvanāti ettha “yañhī”tiādi adhikārattā, gamyamānattā ca na vuttaṃ, etena ca abhijātiyaṃ dhammatāvasena uppajjanakavisesā sabbabodhisattānaṃ sādhāraṇāti dasseti. Pāramitānissandā hi te.

Referring to the introductory verse spoken by the Venerable Ānanda Thera in the Nāḷaka Sutta of the Suttanipāta, the compiler of the commentary has said: ‘suvaṇṇadaṇḍā vītipatanti cāmarāti etthā’. Indeed, ‘etthā’ means ‘in this verse’. However, because the raising of the chowrie is not mentioned in the Mahāpadāna Sutta, the statement should be understood in that way. Indeed, in accordance with what is mentioned there, here it speaks of the state of being a preliminary sign. A camara is a special kind of deer. From its tail they make a tail-fan, which is a royal insignia. That which belongs to it is a cāmarī. Its raising was spoken of thus; therefore, it is called ‘the aforesaid raising of the chowrie’ (vuttacāmarukkhepo). ‘For the attainment of the excellent, stainless, white parasol of liberation through Arahantship’ means for the attainment of the excellent, stainless, white parasol called the attainment of the fruit of Arahantship. In ‘sattamapadūpari’ (above the seventh step), the word ‘pada’ denotes a footstep; therefore, the meaning is ‘above the seventh footstep’. The knowledge of omniscience itself, because of its unimpeded movement everywhere, is unobstructed; to show this, he said, ‘for the attainment of the unobstructed knowledge of omniscience’. In ‘Thus this Blessed One…pe…the state of being a preliminary sign’, ‘yañhi’, etc., is not stated because it is the topic under discussion and is understood. And by this, it is shown that at birth, by the power of natural law, the special occurrences are common to all Bodhisattas, for they are the results of the perfections.

Porāṇāti aṭṭhakathācariyā.
